```mermaid
flowchart LR
  F[Frozen licensed fixture and manifest] --> N[Existing native runner and policies]
  N --> S[Existing native metrics and sinks]
  N --> C[Monitor extension: actual ranking and schedule]
  F --> R[Independent event replay]
  C --> R
  R --> P[Validated partial or completed pilot report]
  P --> A[Existing ArtifactWriter and manifests]
  P --> E[Descriptive evidence and insufficient-evidence adoption]
```



### FILE: docs/point-in-time-observations.md

# Point-in-time CI observations and decision signals

COLEMAN 4.2 implements
[#258](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/258). CI durations/outcomes
retain their original availability and revision lineage, so later corrections do
not rewrite the information used by an earlier decision. The base package needs
no provider SDK, credential, hosted service or optional MCP dependency.

Install the wheel attached to [COLEMAN 4.2](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/tag/v4.2.0),
or build a development wheel from reviewed source. Run examples outside the
checkout. [ADR 001](decisions/001-point-in-time-observations.md) records the
module/dependency/extension decisions.

## Observation and revision contract

`ObservationRevision` schema v1 contains protected `TemporalObservation` metadata,
a logical entity ID, first local `received_at`, explicit predecessor `supersedes`
and a typed #251 `Measurement`. Event, source availability and first receipt are
separate instants. Effective availability is their later availability/receipt;
receipt cannot precede declared source availability. Source/local clocks must be
comparable; clock disagreement is rejected, never silently adjusted.

`ObservationHistory` holds at most 4,096 supplied revisions per snapshot. Providers
must preserve all build/job/stage/test/variant dimensions needed to prevent logical
collisions. Measurement names/units/meaning, entity, event/group and target interval
stay stable across a lineage. Revisions can change values and missingness, with
explicit availability. Each lineage has one root and one successor per revision;
missing parents, cycles, forks and conflicting duplicates fail. Identical retries
are idempotent, including their unchanged **first** receipt time. Duplicate payloads
are compared by canonical serialized content. COLEMAN JSON v1 preserves signed
float zero: `0.0` and `-0.0` for one revision key are conflicting representations,
not an input-order-dependent choice. Existing domain JSON semantics are unchanged.

`history.as_of(cutoff)` selects one latest eligible member per logical observation.
Cutoffs are inclusive. Explicit lineage orders ties; revision names are never
lexically ranked. A newer revision can arrive before its predecessor; a late
older delivery cannot replace it. Unknown/unavailable values retain their states
rather than reviving an obsolete earlier value.

For the issue's CI fixture, event time is `10:00:00Z`, r1 becomes available at
`10:00:02Z`, and r2 at `10:05:00Z`:

| Query cutoff | Visible revision |
| --- | --- |
| 10:00:01Z | None |
| 10:00:03Z | r1 |
| 10:05:00Z | r2 |

A receipt later than source availability delays visibility further. Adding or
changing a valid future revision cannot change the earlier query or its fingerprint.
Whole-history hashes intentionally change on append; selected-view hashes identify
only the declared source/version, cutoff and selected eligible content.

Providers attest completeness and source identity. An isolated serialized
`ObservationSnapshot` checks one-row-per-observation and availability; it cannot
prove that an upstream provider supplied every revision. `as_of` establishes
selection for the complete bounded history actually supplied. No stream database,
tombstone protocol, multi-parent merge or implicit provider import is introduced.

All instants reuse the existing aware UTC time contract and Python datetime's
microsecond resolution. Providers must declare rounding/rejection for finer source
clocks before normalization. No local timezone, numeric epoch unit or host clock is
inferred. Context/variant observations sharing executions are not independent data.

## Frozen training and honest signals

`prepare_training` queries at **min(information cutoff, declared train_end)**,
selects the named measurement, and reuses `TemporalPlan` eligibility/purging.
Target intervals must also end by this actual information cutoff, even if the
predeclared training window ends later. Serialized training artifacts recheck the
same effective boundary. The model records temporal exclusions without retaining excluded labels. An eligible but
unknown/unavailable training value fails; no mean-zero imputation or silent
complete-case fit occurs. Later validation/test labels and post-training
corrections cannot refit the frozen model.

Fitting only inspects the available past view. The complete later evaluation must
still apply the existing protected cross-fold group gate; future group membership
cannot rewrite a past feature. Seeds and repeated synthetic builds never become
independent observations.

`fit_quantity_mean` implements a simple baseline for nonnegative physical
quantities, not a claim of superior forecasting. Inputs must be finite, between
0 and 10^12, in exactly the declared units/meaning. It sums exact rational forms
of the #251 binary64 inputs and rounds the mean **up to 10^-9 of that unit**,
independently of Decimal context. For example, `(0, 1, 0)` gives `0.333333334`.
Binary64 `0.1` is slightly above mathematical 0.1 and therefore rounds up to
`0.100000001`; this rule does not recover an unknown original decimal spelling.
Exact rounded `Quantity` values remain in the model; signal values declare their
binary64 projection. There is no implicit seconds/milliseconds conversion.

A `QuantityMeanModel` retains eligible training evidence, temporal protocol,
freeze time, means, logical observation counts and latest event times. Reads
rederive those values and reject tampering. Counts describe observations; they
are not confidence estimates or proof of independence.

A `DecisionSignal` carries request/target identity, decision time, information
cutoff, closed future target interval, interpreted measurement, explicit
availability, producer/model versions, eligible-source/model fingerprints and the
freshness rule when used. Its cutoff cannot exceed decision time, its target
cannot precede the decision and its model must already be frozen. Units and
meanings remain explicit for null values too.

| Availability | Measurement status | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| available | observed | 0 | A real available estimate/score of zero |
| missing | unknown | null | Insufficient eligible history |
| stale | unavailable | null | Source event is too old at the decision |
| unavailable | unavailable | null | Producer declares unavailable information |
| not_applicable | not_applicable | null | Explicitly inapplicable signal |

The mean helper emits available, missing or stale signals. Age is decision time
minus latest **event** time; a newly received correction does not make an old event
fresh. Maximum age uses `EVENT_AGE_SECONDS`, with equality still fresh. The rule
is stored in the signal and enters specification/logical identity. The resolved
cutoff/horizon also enter specification identity, so changing context cannot be
silently treated as an identical domain-record replay. A null generic
freshness rule means unspecified by that producer, not guaranteed fresh forever.

The generic signal supports signed priority scores when their declared lower
bound permits them. A negative score remains negative. A priority score is not a
calibrated probability, reward, causal effect or hypothesis-test result.
Generic readers validate schema/chronology/metadata without executing arbitrary
producer code. For a serialized mean signal, call `model.verify_signal(signal)`
to check the complete canonical value, status, parameters and provenance against
its frozen training evidence before use, including signed-zero representation.

## Complete installed library example

This repository-owned synthetic fixture uses test occupancy seconds. The future
correction cannot influence the earlier query or frozen duration estimate.

```python
from datetime import datetime
from decimal import Decimal

from coleman.artifacts import ArtifactWriter
from coleman.evaluation.protected import TemporalPlan
from coleman.observations import (
    EVENT_AGE_SECONDS, DecisionSignal, ObservationHistory, ObservationRevision,
    SignalRequest, fit_quantity_mean, prepare_training, publish_model, publish_signal,
)
from coleman.selection import Quantity, UnitSemantics

seconds = UnitSemantics(unit="s", meaning="test-runner-occupancy-v1")
r1 = ObservationRevision.model_validate({
    "schema_version": 1,
    "metadata": {
        "observation_id": "build-2:test-a:duration", "revision_id": "r1",
        "group_id": "build-2", "event_at": "2026-01-02T10:00:00Z",
        "available_at": "2026-01-02T10:00:02Z",
    },
    "entity_id": "test-a", "received_at": "2026-01-02T10:00:02Z", "supersedes": None,
    "measurement": {
        "name": "ci_duration", "value": 3.0, "unit": "s", "meaning": seconds.meaning,
        "direction": "none", "status": "observed", "minimum": 0.0,
    },
})
r2 = ObservationRevision.model_validate({
    **r1.model_dump(), "supersedes": "r1", "received_at": "2026-01-02T10:05:00Z",
    "metadata": {**r1.metadata.model_dump(), "revision_id": "r2", "available_at": "2026-01-02T10:05:00Z"},
    "measurement": {**r1.measurement.model_dump(), "value": 9.0},
})
history = ObservationHistory(schema_version=1, source_id="owned-ci-demo", source_version="1", revisions=(r1, r2))
assert history.as_of(datetime.fromisoformat("2026-01-02T10:00:01Z")).observations == ()
assert history.as_of(datetime.fromisoformat("2026-01-02T10:00:03Z")).observations == (r1,)
plan = TemporalPlan.model_validate({
    "train_end": "2026-01-02T10:00:03Z", "validation_end": "2026-01-02T11:00:00Z",
    "test_end": "2026-01-04T00:00:00Z",
})
training = prepare_training(
    history, plan, information_cutoff=plan.test_end,
    measurement_name="ci_duration", input_semantics=seconds,
)
model = fit_quantity_mean(training, frozen_at=datetime.fromisoformat("2026-01-02T10:00:04Z"))
request = SignalRequest.model_validate({
    "schema_version": 1, "decision_id": "build-3", "entity_id": "test-a",
    "decided_at": "2026-01-03T10:00:00Z", "information_cutoff": "2026-01-03T10:00:00Z",
    "target_start": "2026-01-03T10:00:00Z", "target_end": "2026-01-03T10:01:00Z",
})
signal = model.signal(request, maximum_event_age=Quantity(value=Decimal(86400), semantics=EVENT_AGE_SECONDS))
assert signal.measurement.value == 3.0
assert signal.availability == "available"
writer = ArtifactWriter("point-in-time-library-artifacts")
publish_model(model, writer)
path = publish_signal(signal, writer)
assert model.verify_signal(DecisionSignal.from_json(path.read_bytes())) == signal
```

To add an authorized provider, implement `ObservationProvider.load_history()` in
an external adapter package and return typed `ObservationHistory`. Establish
source-specific identities, units, clock resolution and immutable first receipts;
retain complete bounded lineage and bound raw payloads before decoding. The core
never loads a provider from a name, URI or credential. `OfflineObservationProvider`
revalidates an already supplied owned history without I/O.

## Real native TCPCI and recovery

Copy [`ci.py`](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v4.6.0/examples/point-in-time/ci.py)
outside the checkout and run `python ci.py native-observation-demo` from the
installed 4.6.0 wheel or source build. It fits owned historical quantities at a frozen
training cutoff before decisions, then runs three constructed native CI copies using
`run_with_extension`, native Parquet results, RNFail and existing checkpoints.

The native first-build shuffle remains a warmup. On the next two builds, fresh
estimates produce t2/t3/t1; stale estimates retain the full base order t1/t2/t3.
The policy reads logical test names and frozen historical signals, without using
current realized durations/verdicts as predecision estimates. The historical and
current durations intentionally differ. No required test is removed by fallback.
This is functional offline replay, with no prospective execution, savings,
calibration or superiority claim.

Models/signals use existing immutable `ArtifactWriter` publication in
`observation-models/` and `decision-signals/`. Matching named domain sidecars enter
the existing sink before checkpoint advancement. Native manifests discover those
families. Signal paths use the stable logical ID: identical retries succeed and
changed content for that ID conflicts. Models use their content fingerprints.
Logical identity derives from dataset/policy/reward/experiment, excluding
native runtime attempt suffixes, retry clocks and worker IDs. Content digests are
deterministic. A changed freshness policy changes specification identity. Domain
sinks retain their existing conflicting-logical-record checks.

The same owned output can resume with `python ci.py native-observation-demo`.
Immutable input/configuration/actual RunSpec proofs must match before loading a
checkpoint. Checkpoints live in the existing native run directory; only trusted
local checkpoints created by the example may be loaded. Unknown output roots,
changed inputs/parameters/specs and pre-existing symlinks fail before native use.
Local path checks assume no hostile concurrent filesystem mutation, not an OS
sandbox. Concurrent native invocations must use separate output roots: the existing
checkpoint store does not coordinate simultaneous writers of one logical execution.
Existing native pickle/checkpoint durability limits remain unchanged.

Regression tests interrupt after signal publication, after a synchronous domain
record commit, and after checkpoint commit, then resume through the real store. Accepted
signals remain complete; retry reuses the same logical signal path/content digest
and domain records are not duplicated. Reopened/concurrent Parquet writers now use distinct per-flush
filenames even within one PID/second, preserving previously committed native rows.
Legacy Parquet filenames were already operational/non-deterministic; deterministic
mathematical identities belong to versioned models/signals/domain records.

Unknown/future/missing versions and duplicate JSON keys fail closed. Existing
native artifacts keep their readers/meaning; there is no automatic migration or
silent conversion to observation histories. Same-content publication is
idempotent; conflicts/I/O errors propagate and incomplete temporary files never
become completed artifacts. There is no additional checkpoint or stream store.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  P[Authorized provider or owned offline fixture] --> H[Typed bounded revision history]
  H --> A[As-of source availability and first receipt]
  A --> T[Existing protected training eligibility]
  T --> M[Frozen simple quantity model]
  M --> S[Versioned estimate or explicit missing/stale signal]
  S --> N[Existing native extension policy and conservative fallback]
  S --> D[Existing domain sidecars and immutable artifacts]
  N --> C[Existing native checkpoint]
  D --> C
```



### FILE: docs/prospective-shadow.md

# Frozen CI shadow evaluation

`coleman.shadow` records pre-outcome recommendations while required CI continues
running its full test suite. It separates raw CI observations, application receipt,
actual resource accounting, counterfactual subset costs, operational health and
research conclusions. It reuses [point-in-time observations](point-in-time-observations.md),
[resource accounting](resource-replay.md), [domain records](domain-results.md),
immutable artifacts and native runner/checkpoint interfaces.

Available from COLEMAN 4.3. Build this revision or use the verified 4.4 release
wheel for these examples; the 4.2 wheel does not contain this module. No credentials,
hosted service, external CI trigger or optional MCP package is needed.

## Complete typed library example

This owned synthetic fixture declares one failing required test and two identical
predeclared candidates. It demonstrates contracts and recovery, not improvement
or prospective evidence. All source UTC instants are synthetic. Host monotonic
nanoseconds are explicit inputs, not inferred from UTC:

```python
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from coleman.artifacts import ArtifactWriter
from coleman.evaluation.protected.temporal import TemporalObservation, TemporalPlan
from coleman.observations import ObservationRevision
from coleman.resources import RUNNER_MS, ResourceAmount, ResourceEstimate, ResourceRequest, TestEstimate
from coleman.results.domain import Measurement, fingerprint
from coleman.shadow import (
    BuildClosed, BuildOpened, CandidateDecision, FrozenCandidate, HostClock,
    ShadowProtocol, ShadowReport, ShadowSource, ShadowState, SourceStatus,
    TestFeedback, load_shadow_state, publish_shadow_state, verify_shadow_checkpoint,
)

def at(value):
    return datetime.fromisoformat(value)

def amount(ms):
    return ResourceAmount(value=ms, semantics=RUNNER_MS)

start = at("2026-01-02T10:00:00Z")
source = fingerprint({"owned": "single-test-contract-example-v1"})
plan = TemporalPlan(train_end=at("2025-12-31T00:00:00Z"),
                    validation_end=at("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"),
                    test_end=at("2026-01-09T00:00:00Z"))
candidates = tuple(FrozenCandidate(
    candidate_id=name, policy_version="fixed-order-v1", model_fingerprint=source,
    feature_fingerprint=source, selection_version="serial-prefix-v1",
    fallback_version="no-action-v1", budget=amount(1001), shared_setup_reserve=amount(0),
) for name in ("base", "candidate"))
protocol = ShadowProtocol(
    schema_version=1, experiment_id="owned-single-test", source=ShadowSource(
        source_id="owned-ci", source_version="1", schema_fingerprint=source,
        authorization_reference="urn:coleman:owned-example", license_id="MIT",
        clock_assumption="synthetic-source-and-host-fixture-v1", evidence_basis="functional_offline",
    ), benchmark_fingerprint=source, frozen_at=plan.validation_end, temporal_plan=plan,
    candidates=candidates, baseline_id="base", independent_groups=(), independence_justification=None,
    minimum_observation_days=7, minimum_builds=2, minimum_independent_groups=2,
    minimum_recall=1.0, minimum_net_saving_ms=1, actual_build_capacity=amount(2000),
    maximum_silence_ns=60 * 10**9, maximum_source_lag_seconds=60, maximum_pending=4,
    maximum_events=64, maximum_event_bytes=65536, maximum_journal_bytes=1048576,
)
cost = ResourceEstimate(amount=amount(1000), source_fingerprint=source,
                        observed_at=plan.train_end, available_at=plan.validation_end,
                        valid_until=plan.test_end)
state = ShadowState(schema_version=1, protocol=protocol)
heartbeat = SourceStatus(event_id="connected", available_at=start, connected=True)
state = state.ingest(heartbeat, HostClock(session_id="process-a", tick_ns=0, utc_at=start))
decisions = tuple(CandidateDecision(
    candidate_id=c.candidate_id, model_fingerprint=c.model_fingerprint,
    request=ResourceRequest(schema_version=1, decision_id="build-2",
        configuration_fingerprint=fingerprint(c.model_dump(mode="json")), decided_at=start,
        capacity=c.budget, tests=(TestEstimate(test_id="test-a", estimate=cost),), ranking=("test-a",)),
    decision_overhead=amount(1), shared_setup_reserve=c.shared_setup_reserve,
    overhead_interpretation="occupied_runner",
) for c in candidates)
opened = BuildOpened(event_id="build-2:opened", build_id="build-2", logical_build_id="build-2",
    group_id="owned-project", decided_at=start, target_end=start + timedelta(seconds=60),
    required_ids=("test-a",), actual_estimate=cost, decisions=decisions)
state = state.ingest(opened, HostClock(session_id="process-a", tick_ns=1, utc_at=start))
finished = start + timedelta(seconds=1)
feedback = TestFeedback(event_id="build-2:test-a:completed:r1", build_id="build-2", test_id="test-a",
    revision=ObservationRevision(schema_version=1, entity_id="test-a", supersedes=None,
        received_at=finished, metadata=TemporalObservation(observation_id="build-2:test-a",
            revision_id="r1", group_id="owned-project", event_at=finished, available_at=finished),
        measurement=Measurement(name="ci_failure", value=1.0, unit="1",
            meaning="ci-test-failure-indicator-v1", direction="none", status="observed")),
    occupancy=amount(1000))
receipt = HostClock(session_id="process-a", tick_ns=2, utc_at=finished)
state = state.ingest(feedback, receipt)
closed = BuildClosed(event_id="build-2:closed", build_id="build-2", available_at=finished,
    dispatch_occupancy=amount(1), shared_setup_occupancy=amount(0), queue_elapsed=None, setup_elapsed=None)
state = state.ingest(closed, HostClock(session_id="process-a", tick_ns=3, utc_at=finished))
assert state.ingest(feedback, receipt).to_json() == state.to_json()
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    writer = ArtifactWriter(directory)
    checkpoint = publish_shadow_state(state, writer)
    assert verify_shadow_checkpoint(checkpoint, protocol, writer).fingerprint == state.fingerprint
    assert load_shadow_state(protocol, writer).to_json() == state.to_json()
report = ShadowReport(schema_version=1, state=state)
assert report.evidence().outcome == "inconclusive"
assert report.evidence().forward_logical_builds == 0
assert report.evidence().actual_known_required_runner.value == 1001
assert all(row.net_saving.value == 0 for row in report.findings())
```

Persist each returned state before acknowledging the upstream source. In an actual
consumer, publish the opening before requesting any feedback; the compact example
above keeps transitions in memory to show the complete contract. Fingerprints bind
reviewed configurations; they do not prove that arbitrary producer code computed
an honest model or used the declared features.

The core currently supports `selection_version="serial-prefix-v1"` and two frozen
fallback versions: `no-action-v1` binds `ResourceRequest.fallback="no_action"`;
`full-suite-if-estimated-feasible-v1` binds `fallback="full_suite"`. A decision
cannot substitute another fallback, even when priority is currently available.
Full-suite fallback still requires every eligible estimate, known inference and
the declared setup reserve to fit the same budget. Unknown selection/fallback
versions fail closed rather than executing another algorithm under their names.
Each non-null request estimate must carry the frozen candidate's
`feature_fingerprint` as its `source_fingerprint`, binding the reviewed feature
and cost-estimation evidence. Swapping provenance requires a new frozen experiment;
missing estimates remain unavailable and cannot acquire invented provenance. This
check does not prove arbitrary producer computations: verify their evidence/model
before publication, as the native example does for its owned configuration.

## Real native full-suite workflow

Build and install the wheel in a separate Python 3.14 environment. Copy
[`examples/prospective-shadow/ci.py`](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/examples/prospective-shadow/ci.py)
to an empty workspace and run it twice:

```bash
python ci.py shadow-output
python ci.py shadow-output
```

The example uses `run_with_extension`, `build_environment`, the native policy and
monitor hooks, actual scheduling/evaluation, domain sidecars and
`LocalCheckpointStore`. Warmup plus two required suites execute all three tests
in base order. Shadow selections never change that order. The optional final
forecast creates no extra evidence build.

The model is an actual frozen `QuantityMeanModel` fitted through protected
`prepare_training` to prior failure indicators. Signals are verified against that
model. Only test IDs, historical model and prior duration estimates enter the
candidate; current durations/verdicts cannot affect its sealed recommendation.
A historical binary mean is not asserted to be a calibrated failure probability.
The complete future Parquet input is bound separately to native input provenance;
its digest is not a candidate feature or future-outcome protocol component.

Each candidate has the same 4,000 ms nominal budget. The selector deducts its
measured inference cost and the frozen shared-setup reservation first. The fixture
explicitly declares zero shared setup; it does not assume that real CI setup is
free. Whole-native prioritization elapsed and per-candidate inference elapsed are
rounded upward to integer milliseconds and labeled one-runner occupancy proxies.
They are not provider bills. Whole-native dispatch includes shadow journal/model
work; storage and monitoring overhead are not attributed separately to each
candidate. The subset comparison is therefore not a complete operational cost
comparison. Actual test work is 7,000 ms per required suite, plus
the native dispatch proxy. Counterfactual subset cost is selected source work plus
one actual shared setup plus candidate inference. Shared setup is never removed
per test. Queue/setup elapsed remain separately unknown.

The first measured native source batch is immutable before event publication.
Restart reuses its timing even when the runner checkpoint did not advance.
Subsequent admissions and domain records precede native checkpoint advancement.
The completed rerun has identical report/source artifacts and logical record
counts. Timing varies between fresh executions; replay preserves the first actual
measurement rather than pretending that wall time is reproducible.

The report remains **inconclusive**: two synthetic builds on one day, seven days
required, zero genuine forward builds, no justified independent groups. Repeating
the fixture, retrying builds or changing synthetic dates cannot establish value.

## Source admission, clocks and containment

- `HostClock.utc_at` is first validated application admission. `tick_ns` is a local
  monotonic witness scoped to `session_id`. UTC receipts cannot reverse; ticks
  cannot reverse within a session, including when a previously admitted session
  recurs after another session or checkpoint restoration. A new process requires a fresh source status
  before new recommendations. Never subtract monotonic ticks across sessions.
- Original provider `received_at`, event time and availability remain untouched
  in `TestFeedback.revision`. The derived `ObservationHistory` has a distinct
  `:shadow-admission-v1` source identity and uses application admission as its
  usable receipt. Late validation cannot make a label available retrospectively.
- Freshness requires a new, ordered, connected source status whose UTC lag is
  within policy, plus bounded local monotonic silence. Duplicate payloads refresh
  neither clock nor evidence. Old heartbeats cannot roll back the source watermark.
- Missing causal parents, unknown builds/tests, conflicting lineages, changed
  occupancy and invalid frozen bindings enter bounded typed quarantine and stop
  recommendations. Rejected malformed inputs, clock reversals, byte/event limits
  and same-ID changed payloads raise `ValueError` without changing prior state.
  Unsupported causal repair requires a reviewed new experiment; v1 does not
  silently reorder parents or auto-release quarantined observations.
- Out-of-order independent physical completions are supported. Application order
  books work; original source chronology remains available. Corrections require
  the existing lineage contract, preserve original as-of history and never charge
  work twice. V1 allows label changes with identical occupancy only. Unknown-to-known
  occupancy is also an unsupported accounting correction, not a free adjustment.
- An explicit closure with missing feedback or unknown occupancy keeps reservation
  and accounting pending. Late required feedback can finish it. Once physical work
  is known complete, unused reservation is released before closure overhead is
  charged, avoiding a transient accounting overrun from already-unused resources. Unknown labels can
  settle known work but cannot score complete quality evidence. No closed build is
  assumed successful merely because its job ended. Closures before upstream start
  or known physical completion, and physical completion after upstream closure,
  are quarantined; late admission and label corrections with consistent original
  event times remain supported.
- Actual resource overruns are retained without clipping. Recall/resource breaches
  stop further recommendations; actual upstream required work is still observed.
  Observation-only openings have empty decisions and cannot manufacture candidate
  results. This analytical consumer cannot cancel or enforce external CI jobs.
- Operational states are `healthy`, `stopped`, `recovering`. Research outcomes are
  `pass`, `fail`, `inconclusive`; adoption remains `insufficient_evidence`.
  `ShadowReport` describes the last committed receipt. Query
  `state.operational(current_host_clock)` for current health after silence/restart.

## Evidence and limits

Freeze the source/schema/authorization, benchmark identity, temporal windows,
candidate/model/features/selection/fallback definitions, identical budgets/setup
reservations, trial registry, outcome definition, minimum days/builds/groups,
independence justification, quality/practical thresholds and stopping policy before
collection. Changes produce another experiment fingerprint and cannot inherit old
protected outcomes as untouched evidence.

Only complete required labels support membership recall. Each build is scored at
the earliest of its frozen target end, the study test end and the last application
admission. Later corrections remain in raw history but cannot rewrite that
protected finding or introduce a post-window sticky research-risk breach. Zero failures makes
recall `not_applicable`, not one. A passed test has observed zero, an unknown or
unavailable label has null with its status, and missing work remains null. Negative
net savings remain valid adverse results. All quantities reject nonfinite values;
occupied time requires bounded nonnegative integer milliseconds and exact unit
semantics. No conversion between elapsed queue/setup and runner occupancy occurs.

Days/builds use distinct logical CI identity and the first attempt's decision date;
seeds, retries and corrections add no independent units. Source groups count only
when predeclared with an external justification. Even sufficient descriptive gates
provide no IID inference, confidence interval, causal saving or automatic promotion.
Positive practical savings must be demonstrated; zero savings cannot pass. Partial,
censored, quarantined or insufficient evidence stays inconclusive.

V1 is bounded to 4,096 admissions, 256 required tests per build, 16 candidates,
128 quarantined events, 256 signals per decision, 256 KiB source events and 16 MiB
admitted journal payload, with stricter frozen per-experiment limits. Protocols are
limited to 1 MiB at publication and portable serialized state to 20 MiB. Frame
wrappers and compact checkpoint references add bounded per-event storage overhead.
The API revalidates/replays bounded state, so it is a small auditable consumer,
not an unbounded stream processor. Rotate to a newly predeclared experiment when
retention is exhausted; v1 does not evict deduplication history.

## Atomic artifacts, concurrency and compatibility

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    F[Frozen protocol and prior model] --> D[Sealed shadow recommendations]
    CI[Unchanged required CI suite] --> S[Immutable original source batch]
    D --> J[Typed admission frames]
    S --> J
    J --> L[Existing exact resource ledger]
    J --> O[Application as-of observation history]
    J --> C[Compact journal-prefix reference]
    C --> N[Per-build domain sidecar]
    L --> N
    N --> K[Existing native checkpoint]
    L --> R[Final observed work and modeled subset report]
    O --> R
    K --> R
```

`ArtifactWriter` atomically publishes immutable protocol headers and ordinal,
hash-linked `shadow-journals/<protocol-digest>/frames/NNNN.json`. A complete frame
is the event commit point. A compact `checkpoints/NNNN.json` verifies its prefix;
recovery also reads committed later frames after a crash before checkpoint-ref
publication. Temporary files and incomplete references are never completed events.
Identical concurrent writers converge; different payloads for an ordinal conflict.
The caller reloads and reconciles its durable source after a conflict. There is no
mutable latest pointer, distributed leader election or transaction across native
rows, source batches and domain sidecars. Local artifact filesystem assumptions and
ancestor-directory power-loss limits remain those of the existing writer.

The existing manifest inventories shadow headers, frames, checkpoint references,
source batches and reports within its root. The native example keeps per-build
families in the native run root and publishes the final study report beside it,
after the runner returns. Call `coleman.manifest.generate_manifest` on the outer
output directory to inventory that report together with the native child artifacts.
A frame records an admission, a checkpoint records a
prefix, and neither asserts that a study has completed or evidence has passed.
Reports live in `shadow-reports/<content-digest>.json`; logical experiment identity
is the complete frozen protocol fingerprint, distinct from changing state digests.
JSON serialization is canonical, finite and deterministically hashed.

All new portable contracts require explicit integer `schema_version=1`; missing,
future/unknown versions, extra fields and duplicate JSON keys fail closed. There
is no implicit migration. Legacy native scheduling rows, v3.2 artifacts and older
domain records retain their existing readers and meanings. They have no prospective
protocol or first admission provenance, so cannot be relabeled as shadow evidence.
Future migration must be explicit, versioned and preserve the original bytes and
provenance; unsupported occupancy corrections remain an explicit v1 limitation.

## Forward-run protocol and empty report template

Before an actual authorized forward run, record and review:

1. Source owner permission/reference, public redistribution license, retention
   policy, source schema, stable build/test/retry IDs and correction guarantees.
2. Provider event/availability/first receipt mapping, host UTC synchronization
   assumption, process session/tick generation, lag/silence limits, disconnect and
   backlog behavior, partial/censored feedback and collection failure procedure.
3. Frozen candidates and actual executable/configuration/model hashes, feature
   availability audit, historical training/validation cutoffs, complete baseline,
   trial registry, equal resource budget/setup reservation and independent source
   groups with defensible dependence analysis.
4. Untouched future window, minimum distinct days/builds/groups, required-label
   visibility, practical thresholds, stopping rules, immutable artifact roots,
   source acknowledgments and native checkpoint/fault-recovery rehearsal.
5. Independent required-CI execution: collection errors and containment cannot
   suppress required jobs. Start collection only after protocol freeze. Record
   all trials, failures, negative findings, costs and missing observations.

Deliver the following report with **uncollected fields left unavailable**:

| Field | Before collection |
| --- | --- |
| Frozen protocol/source/model digests | Record reviewed digests |
| Owner permission/license/clock references | Record reviewed references |
| Planned and actually observed windows | Planned window; actual unavailable |
| Required/scored/partial/quarantined logical builds | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Genuine forward builds and distinct decision days | 0 / 0 |
| Justified independent groups and dependence caveats | Unavailable until verified |
| Actual runner work, setup/queue elapsed, inference cost | Unavailable; do not enter zero |
| Baseline/candidate recall and modeled signed savings | Unavailable |
| Operational source state and recovery incidents | Record current state/incidents |
| Research outcome / adoption | Inconclusive / insufficient evidence |
| Raw artifacts, missingness, exclusions and limits | Link complete audit; explain gaps |

This template and the offline native fixture are the deliverables here. They do
not claim that any live prospective CI observations have already been collected.



### FILE: docs/protected-evaluation.md

# Protected evaluation for CI decisions

Existing COLEMAN analysis reports summarize native TCPCI output. A ranking or an
average over repeated seeds is descriptive; it does not establish independent
scientific evidence. This additive library API separates chronological eligibility,
frozen candidate/protocol declarations, recorded holdout access and paired inference.
It uses the [versioned result contract](domain-results.md), existing native runner
extensions, sinks, artifacts and manifests. No scheduling algorithm or legacy
result meaning is replaced.

## Temporal eligibility

```python
from coleman.evaluation.protected import TemporalObservation, TemporalPlan

plan = TemporalPlan.model_validate({
    "train_end": "2026-01-02T23:59:59Z",
    "validation_end": "2026-01-04T23:59:59Z",
    "test_end": "2026-01-06T23:59:59Z",
})
late = TemporalObservation.model_validate({
    "observation_id": "repository-a/build-1",
    "group_id": "repository-a",
    "event_at": "2026-01-02T12:00:00Z",
    "available_at": "2026-01-03T12:00:00Z",
})
assert not plan.training_eligible(late)
assert plan.decide(late).reason == "outcome_not_available"
```

Train is `(-infinity, train_end]`, validation `(train_end, validation_end]`, and test
`(validation_end, test_end]`. Cutoffs must increase strictly. Zoned ISO timestamps
are normalized to UTC; naive/date-only times and numeric epochs/strings fail.
Event time fixes the nominal partition: late labels never move training events
into validation/test. Both label availability and the entire closed target interval
must be within that partition's cutoff. This conservative purge excludes a training
target extending into validation or test, even if an early outcome is already known.

`TemporalPlan.split(tuple_of_metadata)` returns sorted typed decisions with an
eligibility flag and reason (`eligible`, `outside_window`, `outcome_not_available`,
`overlapping_target`). It rejects groups spanning nominal partitions, including late
rows, duplicate revision identities, and revisions changing event/group identity.
Post-cutoff revisions are retained as excluded decisions rather than overwriting
legitimate historical observations. It does not choose or aggregate competing
revisions; a producer must predeclare its point-in-time revision selection.

`plan.observation(mapping)` is a dataset-boundary adapter. Configure `event_field`,
`availability_field`, `group_field`, `observation_field`, `revision_field` and
`target_end_field` for an existing dataset. Required metadata missing from a mapping
raises `KeyError`; invalid values raise Pydantic `ValidationError`. Optional
`target_end` defaults to a point interval at the event, and `revision_id` defaults
to `original`. Other dataset columns stay outside the metadata contract.

## Freeze before protected outcomes

`FrozenCandidate.from_configuration` accepts a complete JSON configuration at the
boundary and stores canonical JSON bytes in an immutable typed object. Include all
hyperparameters, preprocessing/feature definitions, learned-state fingerprints and
external dependency versions used by that candidate. A hash cannot freeze an
undeclared dependency or prove that an external fit did not inspect future labels.

`freeze` takes typed candidates, the canonical dataset fingerprint, the temporal
plan, an `EvaluationProtocol` and a tuple of `ComparisonHypothesis` declarations.
The result is a `FrozenEvaluation`; persist it with `EvaluationAudit.save_freeze`
before running or evaluating the candidates. Changing data, candidates, thresholds,
units, assumptions, plan or family changes its SHA-256 fingerprint. Candidate and
hypothesis declaration order is canonicalized; duplicate/self/reversed/unfrozen
comparisons are rejected. Never add a favorable hypothesis after reading outcomes.

The protocol declares:

- `metric_name`, `unit`, `meaning`, and objective `direction`;
- `independent_unit` and `dependence` (`independent`, `serial`, `clustered`);
- explicit `normal_differences_assumed`, required by the v1 inference method;
- nonnegative `practical_effect` **in the metric's own unit**, family-wise `alpha`,
  and `minimum_units` (default 20, always at least 2);
- a stable `holdout_id`, retained across candidates, protocol revisions and dataset
  revisions exposing the same protected observations.

For NAPFD/APFDc, larger is better and the unit is dimensionless `1`. Native
`cost` is historically named but contains APFDc, not monetary expense. Actual
execution cost needs its own measured unit/meaning and minimization objective.

`named_seed(root_seed, candidate_id, purpose)` hashes canonical named input into
64-bit entropy compatible with NumPy, Polars and Python RNGs. Candidate/worker
ordering does not affect the stream. Use distinct purposes for training, selection,
evaluation or dataset-specific execution. It does not modify existing run IDs,
sweep semantics or legacy native RNG derivation, and does not make repeated seeds
independent evidence. Truncated seeds are reproducibility tools, not unique IDs;
content identities continue to use full SHA-256 fingerprints.

## Access history and interrupted work

`EvaluationAudit(artifact_root)` stores immutable frozen contracts, access receipts
and completed reports through the existing `ArtifactWriter`. `evaluate` reserves
a test/confirmatory access **before invoking the outcome loader**. Every invocation
counts, including attempts whose loader/validation/inference later fails. A retry
after publication cannot claim a previously untouched holdout. Calling
`audit.access` also records train/development, validation/tuning and test/verification
accesses. Any test exposure, including tuning or verification, counts toward reuse.

Keep a **shared durable audit root and stable holdout ID** for every workflow using
the same protected observations. Changing candidates, protocol or dataset fingerprint
does not reset a holdout ID's exposure count. Creating a different root or disguising
the holdout with another ID cannot establish fresh evidence. This is an audit of
calls through these APIs; it is not access control over files, proof of undisclosed
external access, or a cryptographically authenticated tamper seal.

Reservations form a validated ordinal/hash chain. Concurrent processes compete on
atomic create-if-absent publication and retry with a fresh chain snapshot; no lock
file survives interruption. One contender records the first test access. Temporary
files are ignored. Missing internal entries, changed predecessors, corrupt content
and unknown versions fail closed. External removal of an entire history cannot be
detected by that history alone; protect/retain the audit root as part of the research
record. Local hard-link/directory-fsync requirements and power-loss limitations are
the same as [domain artifacts](domain-results.md).

A reservation is an attempted access, not a completed evaluation. `save_report`
requires a matching persisted receipt and frozen contract, then atomically publishes
validated report content. Point estimates must be present for uncertainty or
confirmatory claims, follow the protocol-defined sign (relative tolerance `1e-12`,
zero absolute tolerance) and lie within their reported interval. Report validation
recomputes Holm corrections from the complete frozen raw p-value family (unavailable
tests count as p=1); stored adjusted values must match that deterministic calculation
exactly. Every report embeds its versioned raw records and verifies their logical
keys and content digests. Reading or persisting a report recomputes the complete
frozen method from those records. Scalar agreement permits relative `1e-12` and
absolute `1e-15` numerical variation across compatible libraries; counts, reasons
and conclusions must agree exactly, so a threshold crossing fails closed.
Failed evaluation leaves the attempt and creates no completed report. Replaying
the same report/sink publication is idempotent.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Metadata[Point-in-time metadata] --> Split[Typed split and exclusion decisions]
    Candidates[Complete candidate configurations] --> Freeze[Immutable frozen protocol and family]
    Split --> Freeze
    Freeze --> Runner[Existing native runner extension]
    Runner --> Records[Versioned raw CI measurements]
    Freeze --> Reserve[Durable access receipt before outcome loading]
    Reserve --> Load[Typed protected outcome loader]
    Records --> Load
    Load --> Check[Unit, provenance, pairing and temporal validation]
    Check --> Compare[Paired effects, Holm p-values, simultaneous intervals]
    Compare --> Report[Versioned report with embedded raw records, keys and digests]
    Report --> Artifacts[Existing ArtifactWriter, local sinks and manifest]
```

## Paired method and conservative conclusions

`PairedObservation` links a candidate ID, `TemporalObservation` and `DomainRecord`.
The metadata's group is the independent unit. Exactly one result per candidate/unit
is accepted, with the same metadata across the pair. Repeated seeds/revisions on
one unit raise `ValueError`. Raw record logical keys must also be globally unique
across every candidate and unit in the report, even if candidate names, metadata
labels, provenance, values or content digests differ; use a predeclared
upstream aggregation if replicates
are required. The evaluator verifies frozen dataset/configuration/context
fingerprints, observed availability and metric units/meaning/objective before
calculating a comparison. Unpaired units and incompatible measurements fail.

Version 1 provides paired Student-t inference for a **declared normal population of
independent pair differences**. Serial/clustered units or an undeclared normality
assumption raise `NotImplementedError` before loading outcomes. Adjacent builds from
one real repository generally need a justified dependence model; labeling them with
different seeds does not supply one. No automatic normality or independence detector
is provided. Normality/independence declarations are assumptions to justify in a
study, not certifications inferred by the library.

The implementation applies a one-sample t procedure to paired differences,
equivalent to [SciPy's paired t procedure](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.ttest_rel.html).
Holm's step-down Bonferroni adjustment controls family-wise p-value error across the
entire frozen family; unavailable comparisons remain in that family as p=1.
See the [reference Holm implementation](https://github.com/statsmodels/statsmodels/blob/main/statsmodels/stats/multitest.py).
Intervals use the conservative simultaneous Bonferroni level `1 - alpha/m`, where
`m` is the full family size. They are not unadjusted individual intervals or Holm
intervals. Cross-hypothesis independence is not required by these corrections.

`raw_mean_difference` is candidate minus baseline, in the original metric unit.
`improvement` reverses its sign for minimization. A confirmatory benefit/harm needs
both a Holm-adjusted p-value within alpha and a simultaneous interval entirely
beyond the signed practical-effect threshold. Otherwise the result is inconclusive.
There is **no automatic policy promotion**. Confidence intervals are conditional on
the declared sampling assumptions; p-values are not calibrated failure probabilities
or learning rewards.

Too few units, incomplete outcomes, identical pair differences or nonfinite
uncertainty yield `insufficient_evidence`, with raw signed means retained where
well-defined and unavailable uncertainty represented as null. Unknown outcomes are
not silently removed for a complete-case test. A negative result remains visible.
On a reused holdout, numerical estimates remain available, but a confirmatory
benefit/harm conclusion is suppressed; inspect `confirmatory_eligible` and the
receipt's `prior_test_accesses`. First recorded access means first **within the
complete declared audit history**, not proof that nobody ever saw those data.

Reports contain the complete freeze, access receipt, independent unit IDs, estimates,
conclusions and each embedded raw record's logical key/content digest plus temporal
metadata. The required UTC `completed_at` records when calculation and source
reference assembly finish, after the protected loader and inference. It cannot
predate the access receipt or consumed outcomes. Exported comparison records use
this completion time as `available_at`, never the earlier access request time.
Use the embedded records to verify results against immutable sink records; reserve a
test/verification access before inspecting protected raw outcomes again.
`FamilyReport.domain_records(run_id)` exports typed #251 measurements with explicit
units/signs/unavailable states and no synthetic learning reward. The full report
retains statistical conclusions and access context that a scalar alone cannot convey.

## Runnable installed-package workflow

Install the reviewed wheel, then copy and run
[ci.py](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/examples/protected-evaluation/ci.py)
from a directory outside the repository:

```bash
pip install path/to/coleman.whl
python ci.py ./protected-ci-output
```

The standalone script freezes Greedy/Random RunSpecs before invoking
`run_with_extension`. Four synthetic repository units exercise the real native
runner, RNFail reward, NAPFD metric and Parquet sink. It traces candidate fingerprints
to saved specs, publishes a queryable report and #251 records, and generates a
manifest. It intentionally returns `insufficient_evidence` for four units under a
20-unit minimum. A repeated access is recorded as reuse before the final manifest
is generated, so both receipts appear in its inventory. These synthetic repositories
validate plumbing, not production independence, normality, effectiveness or ROI.

## Compatibility and limits

Frozen/access/report artifacts require integer `schema_version=1`. Duplicate JSON
keys, unknown fields and missing/older/future versions are rejected. No automatic
migration invents missing provenance, units or access history. Legacy native results,
RunSpec IDs, sweep APIs and descriptive reports retain their existing readers and
behavior. Existing domain records can be evaluated only if they already carry the
matching frozen context and candidate configuration; never relabel old artifacts
silently to claim protected evidence.

Version 1 intentionally excludes serial/block/cluster inference, robust/nonparametric
intervals, sequential testing/alpha spending, unknown external state verification,
remote artifact transactions and policy activation. Access-history scanning is
linear in scope history, and contention retries are bounded at 1000 publications.
Reports retain the complete consumed record payload and recompute estimates on
validation; their size and verification cost grow with the paired input. Record
hashes and recomputation establish internal consistency, not authenticity of an
externally supplied dataset or proof of independent sampling.
Keep confirmatory access scarce and predeclared. Larger benchmark/corpus methodology
and mathematical/performance validation remain separate roadmap work.

::: coleman.evaluation.protected

COLEMAN 3.6.1 strengthens the dependency and CI foundations behind reproducible test prioritization and selection. This maintenance release prepares a safer base for the planned 4.0 feature release.

## Security maintenance

- Refresh affected runtime and optional-tool dependencies, including documentation, notebook and release tooling. The complete all-platform lock audit reports **zero known vulnerabilities at the time of validation**, without an advisory ignore list.
- Add a recurring dependency audit that checks every registry package in the committed lock, including extras and packages for other operating systems, and retains machine-readable evidence in CI.
- Pin and verify the CI package-manager download, use locked build/release/audit tools, and disable third-party source builds in Linux CI.
- Protect documentation generation against symlink/path escapes and interrupted output publication.

## Upgrade

Requires Python 3.14 or later:

```sh
python -m pip install --upgrade "https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v3.6.1/coleman-3.6.1-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=ad22e85da1ac9ca42d3e70d10e9ff0d6fecca5f7841f01bcb144a15beffc0646"
```

For contributors, synchronize the updated lock and requested extras. Zensical and Marimo are updated to admit patched transitive dependencies. Native numerical dependency pins and decision/artifact semantics are preserved.

See the [dependency security guide](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/v3.6.1/docs/dependency-security.md) for exact audit commands, scope and platform limitations. A clean advisory query means no known matching reports; it does not prove the absence of undisclosed vulnerabilities.

### FILE: docs/releases/4.0.0.md

# COLEMAN 4.0 — Make every CI budget decision inspectable

CI budgets force a choice: which tests run now, which wait, and what evidence supports that decision? COLEMAN 4.0 makes those choices easier to execute, inspect and reproduce while keeping test-case prioritization and selection at the center of the project.

This release adds a shared, bounded application API and optional local MCP tools, backed by independent mathematical checks. They build on the recent 3.x foundations for versioned results, protected evaluation, finite coverage selection and scenario-based resource allocation.

## New in 4.0

- **One workflow across library, CLI and tools.** Discover approved configurations, submit bounded CI work, inspect status, cancel, retrieve results and export portable evidence. Native COLEMAN services perform the calculation and execution.
- **Independent checks before confident claims.** Small exact reference cases check feasibility, objective values, bounds and ties without calling the production solver. Separate opt-in performance observations record their environment, resource use and limitations.
- **Results with a contract.** Versioned handles and canonical artifacts preserve explicit units, meanings, source identity and provenance. Zero, missing evidence and unavailable results remain distinct.
- **Bounded execution with clear outcomes.** Queue, work, output, retention and worker resource limits have documented behavior. Cancellation, expiry and interrupted writes cannot masquerade as completed jobs. A feasible incumbent remains explicitly different from a proved optimum.
- **Optional tools, a service-free base.** The base wheel needs no MCP SDK, model, credentials or remote service. Configure the optional local stdio adapter once; supported clients can then use its tools directly.

## Try a bounded CI decision

With Python 3.14 or later on Linux or macOS, install this repository's GitHub release wheel in an activated virtual environment:

```bash
python -m pip install 'https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.0.0/coleman-4.0.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=80736c9eb2dc8e16bd1db3c6b30e48b0a3160803b2b35ff86a99fd598541a27c'
coleman application --request '{"schema_version":1,"request_id":"first-ci-decision","spec_id":"weighted-overlap-3","parameters":{"budget":3}}'
```

The packaged synthetic fixture selects **A+C within a 3-second modeled budget** and returns the complete typed result. It demonstrates a checkable decision; it is not a measurement of production CI savings. `native-ci-smoke-v1` exercises the actual TCPCI runner on two synthetic builds.

For MCP, install the same wheel with its optional extra and configure `coleman-mcp` in a local client:

```bash
python -m pip install 'coleman[mcp] @ https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.0.0/coleman-4.0.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=80736c9eb2dc8e16bd1db3c6b30e48b0a3160803b2b35ff86a99fd598541a27c'
```

Use this repository's assets: the bare PyPI name belongs to a different project. Release assets include signed distributions and an SBOM. The [application guide](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/application-api/) includes complete library examples, tool operations, errors and limits.

## Compatibility and evidence

Existing `coleman run`, sweeps, RunSpec workflows and native result/checkpoint interfaces remain available. Existing Parquet fields keep their meanings; old artifacts are not silently reinterpreted. New application bundles use schema version 1 and reject unknown future versions. Portable experiment provenance explicitly declares its redactions and source digest while leaving native result/specification bytes intact.

The release is validated with the full repository suite, native CI workflows, independent reference checks and noneditable installed-wheel tests outside the checkout. Optional MCP lifecycle tests use the real SDK over stdio, offline and without an LLM. Dependency and code-scanning findings are checked before publication; advisory results are time-dependent.

Worker memory and output sampling are local guards with possible transient overshoot, not a hostile-code sandbox. Hosted deployment and durable application-job recovery are outside this release. Export/import retains completed evidence; native checkpoint continuation remains a separate interface.

COLEMAN can report **insufficient evidence**, use a conservative fallback and preserve negative or inconclusive outcomes. Seeds support reproducibility; they do not replace independent observations. No universal algorithm superiority or production wall-clock savings are claimed.

## Explore the release

- [Application API and optional tools](https://jacksonpradolima.github.io/coleman/application-api/)
