Work started with #301 and #302, one reviewed slice at a time. Their compatible
source deliveries were collected in a release branch and published together in
**4.8** through [#316](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/pull/316).
No release number or subtask closure substitutes for an actual source-integrity,
diversity, temporal-admission or scientific evidence gate.

**4.8.0** delivers #301's reviewed ZIP64 selection and complete RTPTorrent
archive/member integrity through [#314](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/pull/314),
plus #302's [full analytical/native Parquet workflow](rtptorrent-parquet-etl.md),
explicit eight-source-job simulation and checkpoint recovery through
[#315](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/pull/315). The signed published
wheel was exercised outside checkout with the actual source cache, native runs
and checkpoint continuation. Remaining source admission, diversity and
confirmatory work continues through the public subtasks. #303's new profiles
preserve all raw/processed stages and use exact context/node bindings, while
retaining explicit missing temporal evidence. Remaining expansion begins with #305.

**4.9.0** publishes the stage-view contracts and three frozen presets: ActiveMQ,
Log4j Ubuntu and Log4j Windows. All raw observations/processed stages remain
analytical evidence; exact context/node bindings select one native view. The
Log4j views share original source identities. Installed real-source workflows
exercise native replay and checkpoints while keeping all temporal blockers.
Existing single-stage LRTS producers, recipes and artifacts retain their semantics.

**4.10.0** publishes #304's [bounded Java fault matrix](java-fault-matrix.md)
on the existing source producer: CLI-13, CLI-51 and an explicitly partial CODEC-65
fixture. Typed plans, raw/context verification, honest incomplete indices and
offline recovery preserve all negative outcomes. Source qualification collected
714 role observations / 357 same-test pairs across two codebases. Controlled
source collection remains separate from admission and policy comparison in #309
onward; the remaining source subtasks follow sequentially.

The existing public adapter issues now have consciously revised generic CI
specifications in **M4 — Point-in-time CI adapters and prospective evaluation**:

- [#258](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/258): point-in-time CI
  observations and versioned decision signals; implemented for 4.2 through existing
  temporal contracts and native extensions.
- [#259](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/259): deterministic CI
  resource accounting and cost-aware replay; implemented for 4.3 on top of #258
  and existing allocation/evaluation/benchmark foundations.
- [#260](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/260): prospective shadow
  evaluation of frozen CI candidates; implemented for 4.3 on top of #259 and
  protected evaluation, without fabricating prospective observations.

Continue the remaining public corpus phases sequentially in later 4.x releases,
with reusable core contracts and CI-centered fixtures. Provider dependencies stay
outside the core. Generic mechanisms, native CI integration, functional recovery
and actual prospective evidence each need explicit validation; offline replay
must never masquerade as a forward observation.

Compatible features use subsequent **4.x minor** versions; compatible fixes use
**4.x patch** versions. A major version requires an actual breaking public contract,
not a large issue count. Release branches may group related reviewed PRs where
needed, while security fixes remain independently shippable. Only implemented,
reviewed, tested behavior belongs in published release notes.

Every slice reuses existing runner, results, artifact and checkpoint interfaces;
includes installed-package examples and independent correctness evidence; passes
local review and repository checks; and receives PR review before integration.
No source admission, performance result, prospective observation, independence
assumption or commercial value is inferred from a planned feature.



### FILE: docs/rtptorrent-parquet-etl.md

# Turn RTPTorrent CI history into Parquet and native TCPCI replays

**COLEMAN 4.8** provides a complete installed-package HikariCP workflow: verified
real archive → full analytical history → bounded native-compatible Parquet →
Random/UCB → checkpoint recovery. Delivered in
[#315](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/pull/315) for
[#302](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/302), it uses the
existing native runner. The 4.7 wheel does not contain this ETL API.

The preset keeps **46,995 source class executions and 1,662 source jobs** in
analytical Parquet. It projects **18 executions from eight declared jobs** into
the existing native runner. The other **46,977 executions remain analytically
available**, with a conserved `outside_jobs` projection reason.

## Install and run outside checkout

Use Python 3.14+ and the verified published wheel. No source checkout, Docker or
MCP SDK is needed for this workflow; the URL pins the actual wheel SHA-256:

```bash
uv venv /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env --python 3.14
uv pip install --python /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env/bin/python "https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.10.0/coleman-4.10.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=b85b6d94fdb48d7f31d580583dfe1be96de2c63f07341b7159d2fbf777639d29"
mkdir -p /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-workspace
cd /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-workspace
```

Download the pinned public archive explicitly. The command supports resuming a
partial operator download; the ETL verifies the complete SHA-256 before parsing:

```bash
curl --fail --retry 3 --continue-at - --max-time 21600 \
  --output rtp-torrent-v11.zip \
  https://zenodo.org/records/4046180/files/rtp-torrent-v11.zip

/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.rtptorrent_etl \
  --archive rtp-torrent-v11.zip \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-data --run > summary.json
```

`--archive` verifies the supplied file even when the expected source is already
cached. Cache and output must be separate and outside Git. Concrete Parquet and
completion destinations are checked before archive acquisition. Source URIs in
the typed recipe are descriptive; the domain opens no URL. The existing small-
source HTTP adapter retains its 300-second cap. The explicit download step keeps
this approximately 5 GB transfer outside that adapter and can resume separately.

Once the cache is populated, repeat the whole conversion/replay **offline**:

```bash
/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env/bin/python -m coleman.transports.rtptorrent_etl \
  --cache /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-source-cache \
  --output /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-data --run > resumed-summary.json
```

The two invocations return the same completion and native run identity. Existing
immutable tables are verified and committed checkpoints are reopened. With the
default two policies and eight modeled rounds, the persisted native result has
**16 rows**, including after continuation. Source verification scans the large
archive again; account for that I/O when planning preprocessing.

The summary contains `completion`, `observations`, `jobs`, `datasets_dir`,
`native_artifacts`, conserved counts and the evidence labels. Native logs go to
stderr so a fresh CLI process can write its JSON summary to stdout. An ETL
completion certifies its three data files; native execution is a subsequent step
with the existing runner's own checkpoint/completion behavior.

## What the files preserve

| File | Scope and semantics |
| --- | --- |
| `observations.parquet` | Every canonical raw project/job/class/source-position execution; exact decimal duration text, observed/unavailable status, seconds and reported-class meaning; nullable method count/failures/errors/skipped; class outcome and one primary projection exclusion |
| `jobs.parquet` | All 1,662 source job labels, source/eligible counts, selected modeled round and status; unavailable logical build ID, event clock and outcome-availability clock remain null |
| `datasets/rtptorrent-hikaricp/features-engineered.parquet` | The 18 eligible records using existing native `BuildId`, `Name`, `Duration`, `CalcPrio`, `LastRun`, `Verdict` and `SourceExecutionId` fields |
| `complete.json` | Last-written versioned recipe/producer/writer provenance, physical file hashes/sizes/row counts, canonical row digest and complete exclusion accounting |

Source `duration` values are **reported class elapsed seconds**, as documented by
the existing [raw-class reader](rtptorrent.md). Analytical `duration_decimal`
retains their exact normalized decimal value as text. Native `Duration` explicitly
projects eligible values to binary64 seconds. An observed zero stays zero; null
with `duration_status=unavailable` stays unavailable. Unknown/not-run outcomes
remain distinct from passes. Failure/error/skipped method counters remain
separate; native verdicts count failing **class executions**, not unique faults.

The physical CSV accounting is:

```text
input_rows = observed_executions + duplicate_rows_excluded
observed_executions = replay_executions + excluded_outside_jobs
                    + excluded_not_run + excluded_unknown_outcome
                    + excluded_unavailable_duration
```

Exact repeated source rows are explicitly counted/excluded; conflicting duplicate
execution keys reject. Repeated classes at distinct positions remain separate.
For selected jobs, not-run precedes unknown outcome, which precedes unavailable
duration as the primary exclusion. Outside-slice records retain their full raw
values and the `outside_jobs` reason; their raw outcome is still inspectable.

## Explicit replay assumptions

The frozen preset selects the first eight numeric job labels with at least two
raw class executions. This criterion uses record cardinality and labels, without
filtering on failures. Selected labels are:

```text
13471129, 13474093, 13476365, 13476403,
13476405, 13476407, 13505429, 13505431
```

Numeric order is an explicit **post-hoc simulation order**. Source job IDs remain
original labels. Native `BuildId` is a local modeled round; it does not assert an
observed logical CI build or join concurrent jobs. No commit/build number,
duration sum or source order becomes an observed clock.

The native model adds reported class seconds serially. It assumes correspondence
between the same class label and its within-job occurrence ordinal across jobs.
Source project/job/class/position execution IDs remain independently preserved and
joinable through `SourceExecutionId`. Occurrences are assigned before eligibility,
so changing an outcome or missing duration cannot rename later occurrences.

The receipt requires
`budget-censored-native-RNFail-zero-nondetection`: detections within budget receive
the existing native reward; other prioritized entries receive zero nondetection
reward, including unscheduled classes. Zero nondetection does not establish a
passing class or full-label feedback. The default run uses Random and UCB,
budget ratio 0.5, seed 42 and one execution per policy. Seed repetitions do not
create independent observations.

Evidence is `posthoc-source-job-serial-simulation`, admission is
`blocked_missing_temporal_evidence`, and generalization is `insufficient_evidence`.
Use this delivery to prepare and reproduce modeled CI experiments. Protected
temporal evaluation needs verified event/outcome clocks and logical build/job
mapping. The source-admission and confirmatory gates in
[#261](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/261) remain open.

## Typed API and a custom bounded slice

The transport loads a metadata-only preset, and the domain exports/verifies it:

```python
from importlib.resources import files
from pathlib import Path

from coleman.application.corpus import run_rtptorrent_replay
from coleman.artifacts import ArtifactWriter
from coleman.corpus import SourceCache
from coleman.corpus.rtptorrent_etl import export_rtptorrent_parquet, validate_rtptorrent_etl
from coleman.corpus.rtptorrent_etl_contracts import RTPTorrentETLReceipt, RTPTorrentETLRecipe

resource = files("coleman.corpus.resources").joinpath("rtptorrent-hikaricp-first-eight-v1.json")
recipe = RTPTorrentETLRecipe.from_json(resource.read_bytes())
cache = SourceCache("/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-source-cache")
completion = export_rtptorrent_parquet(recipe, cache, ArtifactWriter("/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-data"))
receipt = RTPTorrentETLReceipt.from_json(completion.read_bytes())
validate_rtptorrent_etl(receipt, cache, completion.parent)
result = run_rtptorrent_replay(completion, cache, Path("/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-native"))
assert result.run_id
```

For a different reviewed slice, construct an explicit `RTPTorrentETLRecipe` using
one `Zip64SelectionSpec`, its exactly matching existing `RTPTorrentSpec`, a safe
single-component `dataset_id`, at most 16 distinct ascending job labels and the
required feedback declaration. All source observations remain analytical. Unknown
job labels reject. The existing raw-reader limits remain 16 MiB decoded CSV,
50,000 physical rows and 16 KiB per physical line; inputs beyond them reject
without truncation. The published filtered `untreated` baseline is a separate
input and cannot replace the complete raw history.

## Identity, compatibility and recovery

Recipe and completion require integer `schema_version=1` and recipe
`rtptorrent-parquet-source-job-replay-v1`. Missing/future schemas and unknown
assumptions reject. There is no automatic conversion of old native Parquet, LRTS
completions or standalone RTPTorrent datasets into this contract. Existing readers
remain available for those artifacts; create a consciously reviewed new recipe.

The export namespace binds the complete recipe, actual conversion implementation
digest and Polars writer version. Fixed uncompressed Parquet settings bind physical
bytes; `logical_rows_sha256` separately identifies canonical rows. Validation
recomputes actual source membership, conversion, counts and expected physical
bytes. It avoids decoding caller-provided Parquet to certify it. Unknown producer
or writer versions require their recorded implementation and reject certification
under a different one. Metadata-only reading remains distinct from verification.

All three files are immutable before `complete.json` is published last. An
interrupted write may retain individual verified files; retry converges through
the existing writer. Concurrent identical exports converge on the same completion.
Missing/corrupt files or false source/count/provenance claims reject without repair.
Empty native projections remain valid analytical exports and native execution
rejects them explicitly. Trusted local parents and existing filesystem durability
limits apply. No second runner, learning checkpoint or network implementation is
introduced.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Explicit resumed download or existing cache] --> B[Existing SourceCache and bounded ZIP64 profile]
    B --> C[Whole-source and selected-member SHA-256]
    C --> D[Existing complete RTPTorrent raw-class reader]
    D --> E[Typed source-job projection and conserved exclusions]
    E --> F[All observations and jobs in analytical Parquet]
    E --> G[Bounded native-compatible class-execution Parquet]
    F --> H[Immutable last-written ETL completion]
    G --> H
    H --> I[Shared application bridge and existing RunSpec API]
    I --> J[Native Random and UCB with existing checkpoints]
    J --> K[Results plus copied provenance receipt and manifest]
```

## Owned and real installed-package checks

The wheel contains the recipe and owned correctness fixtures. The standalone
example script is a separate repository file: download the exact release-tagged
script and verify its SHA-256, then run twice offline with the installed wheel.
It downloads no foreign dataset:

```bash
cd /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-workspace
curl --fail --location --output owned-ci.py \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/v4.10.0/examples/rtptorrent-parquet/ci.py
/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env/bin/python -c 'import hashlib, sys; from pathlib import Path; sys.exit(0 if hashlib.sha256(Path("owned-ci.py").read_bytes()).hexdigest() == "9b7c8dec20124cefe975d99a2c794a838e791000d3a7cc3046cbcbfaa5c4fd04" else "Example SHA-256 mismatch")'
/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env/bin/python owned-ci.py owned /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-owned-cache
/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-env/bin/python owned-ci.py owned /tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-owned-cache
```

That example preserves eight constructed records, projects four, accounts for
outside/not-run/unknown/unavailable exclusions, and resumes two native rounds with
four result rows. The test suite compares the two-job native NAPFD/APFDc results
with the existing independent exact tiny oracle under the explicit serial model.
The fresh base-wheel regression also exercises the actual real cache when enabled:

```bash
COLEMAN_RTPTORRENT_ETL_REAL_CACHE=/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-source-cache \
  uv run pytest tests/corpus/test_installed_rtptorrent_etl.py --no-cov -q
```

Source pins and data terms are documented in the
[ZIP64 integrity guide](zip64-source-selection.md) and the
[RTPTorrent source assessment](rtptorrent.md). The wheel contains metadata recipes
and owned fixtures; standalone example scripts are downloaded separately above.
Third-party archive/rows stay outside the repository. Dataset terms remain
separate from enclosed subject-code rights, and this workflow reads reported CI observations rather than executing the archived subject repositories.



### FILE: docs/rtptorrent.md

# RTPTorrent: source assessment and bounded class-result conversion

The RTPTorrent adapter in COLEMAN 4.5 converts **raw class-result CSV members**,
using the existing licensed materialization/cache contract. The verified 4.9
wheel retains this reader and includes the complete
[real Parquet/replay workflow](rtptorrent-parquet-etl.md).
RTPTorrent remains blocked from protected temporal evaluation.

An execution is identified by project, job ID, class label and source position.
Repeated class labels remain separate executions. Job IDs are neither logical
build IDs nor timestamps. No commit date, synthetic clock or sum of durations is
substituted for outcome availability.

## Research questions and source decisions

The source audit asks which exact bytes and terms can be pinned, what an observation
means, whether feedback was available before a decision, and which evidence a
baseline table actually retains. It uses the original paper, artifact README and
actual bounded member inspection. This is a focused source-admission assessment,
not a completed systematic literature review or an effectiveness study.

Primary sources checked on 2026-10-15/16 UTC:

- [RTPTorrent 1.1](https://zenodo.org/records/4046180), DOI
  `10.5281/zenodo.4046180`, and its archive README. The provider advertises
  `rtp-torrent-v11.zip`, 5,016,963,482 bytes, MD5
  `1f7fa822b0cf155bd007a94d1a24a336`, and CC BY 4.0 metadata.
- [The authors' MSR 2020 paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3379597.3387458)
  describes the historical Java/Travis corpus and its limitations. The README
  defines class-level duration in seconds and separate method failure/error/skip
  counts, and warns against using concurrent sibling jobs as prior feedback.
- [TravisTorrent's archive notice](https://testroots.github.io/travistorrent-site/page_access/)
  directs users to [Figshare record 19314170](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.19314170)
  and states that raw-log access ended in 2022. The checked record is version 1;
  `final-2017-01-25.csv.gz` has 264,607,174 bytes and provider MD5
  `5d359345fecf0bf47be6edb10b5aae58`.
- [TravisTorrent field documentation](https://testroots.github.io/travistorrent-site/page_dataformat/)
  describes its trigger timestamp. The inspected 66-column CSV header contains
  no explicit completion field. Matching coverage and full dump integrity remain
  unverified. [Travis API documentation](https://docs.travis-ci.com/api/#builds)
  distinguishes start/completion and warns that restarted build duration need
  not equal their difference. These fields cannot silently create outcome times.

The original paper names `travistorrent_8_2_2017.csv` as its metadata join table.
The inspected Figshare dump is `final-2017-01-25.csv.gz`. Their equivalence and
join coverage have not been verified; the accessible snapshot cannot silently
substitute for the one cited in the paper.

The paper also reports 17 negative durations caused by test-runner defects and
notes that clock resolution produces reported zeros. This adapter rejects
negative duration rows rather than repairing them or treating them as unavailable.
A valid reported zero remains zero; it does not prove that execution consumed no
physical time. Changing logging, platforms, components and hardware further
limit cross-job identity and timing comparisons.

The RTPTorrent ZIP64 end record advertises 2,883 entries and 395,312 central-directory
bytes. This exceeds the existing v1 materializer's entry ceiling and ZIP64 policy.
That contract remains unchanged. The implementation delivered in 4.8 through
[#301](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/301) adds a separate
[bounded ZIP64 selection profile](zip64-source-selection.md), without changing
legacy recipes. The profile is available in the published 4.9 wheel. A real
selection recipe still requires the complete archive SHA-256; relabeling a partial
archive as an already validated ZIP would bypass the existing contract.

### Observed source discrepancy

The following **single-project descriptive check** inspected the HikariCP raw
member and its published `untreated` baseline member. It did not pool projects or
estimate independent observations:

| Source member under `rtp-torrent/brettwooldridge@HikariCP/` | Rows | Jobs | Jobs without reported class failures/errors |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `brettwooldridge@HikariCP.csv` | 46,995 | 1,662 | 1,530 |
| `baseline/HikariCP@untreated.csv` | 4,611 | 125 | 0 |

The raw member has 23,693 distinct job/class pairs but 46,995 distinct
job/class/position keys. Collapsing by class would lose executions. The published
baseline is a filtered slice; it cannot stand in for the complete raw history or
establish a zero-failure regime. Counts of source rows without reported failures
are not independent verification that the entire CI job passed.

The independently computed raw-member SHA-256 is
`0ebc3dd28d09227f6aa56698b76c7a217d034aa83318ffc5a75ff8d2d0632687`
for 2,825,388 decoded bytes. The baseline-member SHA-256 is
`ad162fbdd9786db59a30b7bc5625fab19cbac9d5b11e47ca6c1d79b46e041fa9`
for 339,235 decoded bytes. These are **member identities**, not the archive SHA-256.
Initial bounded HTTPS ranges, ZIP metadata and member CRC/size/deflate-EOF checks
informed this research. On 2026-10-16 complete acquisition verified all
5,016,963,482 bytes and the provider MD5; complete source SHA-256 is
`bff52563d75aee2f4bab9693188cdefbfd887dc4bcf63395d49eaff1ecf7b6c1`.
The new [bounded ZIP64 profile](zip64-source-selection.md) verified actual enclosing
membership and repeated offline conversion of the raw HikariCP member. Its frozen
metadata recipe is included in the published 4.9 wheel. The
[real Parquet ETL](rtptorrent-parquet-etl.md) builds on that profile, and source
integrity does not supply missing temporal evidence. No third-party source rows
or archive are committed here.

To reproduce the descriptive counts, obtain the exact 1.1 archive outside Git,
verify its complete bytes against the provider's size/MD5 and compute its SHA-256,
then export the named members with a separately reviewed ZIP64-capable tool. Pin
each decoded member before conversion. Compare raw row counts, distinct job IDs,
distinct job/class and job/class/position keys, and group-level absence of positive
failure/error counts. Do not treat a partial archive or range checksum as proof
of the entire container. Complete archive acquisition/validation is still an
outstanding reproducibility step, not a passing COLEMAN fetch recipe.

**Admission decision: blocked.** The raw layout supplies no event/completion clock
or complete build/job mapping, and repeated class labels lack a disambiguating
module/configuration dimension. A frozen completion/mapping source and explicit
identity/outcome rules are needed before temporal baselines or confirmation. This
is a documented compatibility limit, not a claim that the corpus is permanently
unusable. The registry and all seven uncovered diversity regimes remain unchanged.

## Contract and compatibility

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S[Explicit source bytes and reviewed terms] --> M[Existing pinned materialization]
    M --> C[External immutable source cache]
    C --> R[Bounded raw class-result reader]
    R --> D[Versioned execution dataset and provenance]
    D --> B[Temporal evaluation blocked: clocks and mapping missing]
    D --> A[Source-correspondence check and immutable local artifact]
    F[Owned constructed fixture only] --> I[Isolated serial native projection]
    I --> N[Existing runner and learning checkpoint]
    N --> K[Independent known-answer check]
```

`RTPTorrentSpec` and `RTPTorrentDataset` require integer `schema_version=1` and the
`rtptorrent-class-results-v1` recipe. Missing, legacy, extra-field and future
contracts reject; there is no implicit migration from native Parquet, baseline
CSV, source cards or materialization receipts. Existing artifacts retain their
meaning. `validate_rtptorrent_dataset` recomputes conversion from verified cache
bytes; reading a JSON artifact alone checks invariants, not source correspondence.

The accepted header is exactly:

```text
travisJobId,testName,index,duration,count,failures,errors,skipped
```

| Input | Meaning and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `duration=0` | Observed zero reported class seconds |
| Empty duration | Null with explicit `duration_status=unavailable`, never zero |
| Negative, nonfinite or more than twelve fractional places | Reject conversion |
| Failure/error count greater than zero | Reported failed class; not a unique fault |
| Complete zero failure/error counts with executed methods | Reported passed class |
| All methods skipped or total count zero | Not run; not a pass |
| Incomplete counts without a known failure | Unknown; not a pass |
| Exact repeated execution row | Explicit duplicate exclusion; conserved input count |
| Same project/job/class/position with different values | Reject conflicting identity |
| Repeated class at different positions | Retain separate executions |

Durations use `s` with meaning `rtptorrent-reported-class-elapsed-v1`. They are not
observed runner work or parallel elapsed CI savings. Counts are nonnegative
integers; known failing/error/skipped counts cannot exceed the total. No unique
fault, calibrated probability, flakiness or independence is inferred.
The frozen spec retains duration units even for null values. Non-null duration
quantities require `duration_status=observed`; this source layout supplies no
not-applicable duration encoding, so that status rejects rather than being invented.

Limits are 16 MiB per selected member, at most 50,000 physical data rows, 16 KiB
per physical line and 1,024 characters per field. Duration literals have a
separate 64-character ceiling before Decimal construction. Lower row/line limits may be
frozen in the spec. UTF-8 comma-separated single-line records are required;
multiline quoted labels, malformed records and filtered baseline headers reject.
These are bounded input dimensions, not an operating-system memory sandbox.

## Complete owned example

Install the verified 4.5 release wheel in an activated Python 3.14+ environment.
Run this example outside the checkout. The license below applies
only to this newly authored fixture; never reuse it for downloaded data.

```python
import hashlib
import io
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from pathlib import Path

from coleman.artifacts import ArtifactWriter
from coleman.corpus import MaterializationSpec, SourceCache, load_registry, materialize_source
from coleman.corpus.rtptorrent import convert_rtptorrent_source, publish_rtptorrent_dataset
from coleman.corpus.rtptorrent_contracts import RTPTorrentSpec

payload = (
    b"travisJobId,testName,index,duration,count,failures,errors,skipped\n"
    b"101,owned.Test,0,0,1,0,0,0\n"
    b"101,owned.Test,1,2,1,1,0,0\n"
)
digest = "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
package = MaterializationSpec.model_validate({
    "schema_version": 1,
    "package_id": "owned-rtptorrent-format",
    "archive": "raw",
    "source": {
        "uri": "urn:coleman:owned:rtptorrent-format",
        "version": "1.1",
        "citation": "Repository-authored format-compatible CI fixture",
        "sha256": digest, "size_bytes": len(payload), "availability": "not_verified",
    },
    "license": load_registry().card("ci-serial-boundary-v1").manifest.license,
    "members": [{"name": "classes.csv", "sha256": digest, "size_bytes": len(payload)}],
})
with TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
    root = Path(temporary)
    cache = SourceCache(root / "external-cache")
    receipt = materialize_source(package, cache, lambda: io.BytesIO(payload))
    spec = RTPTorrentSpec(schema_version=1, materialization=receipt,
                         member="classes.csv", project="owned/ci", history="constructed")
    dataset = convert_rtptorrent_source(spec, cache)
    assert len(dataset.executions) == 2 and dataset.repeated_class_executions == 1
    artifact = publish_rtptorrent_dataset(dataset, cache, ArtifactWriter(root / "exports"))
    assert artifact.exists()
    try:
        dataset.require_temporal_evaluation()
    except ValueError as error:
        print(error)  # Expected: no source clock or logical-build mapping.
    else:
        raise AssertionError("A clockless source entered temporal evaluation")
```

For native execution, copy the [complete owned CI example](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/examples/rtptorrent/ci.py)
outside the checkout and run:

```bash
python ci.py owned-ci /absolute/path/outside-git/rtptorrent-cache
python ci.py owned-ci /absolute/path/outside-git/rtptorrent-cache
```

It materializes and converts an owned format-compatible fixture, preserves the
reported green/repeated-class and unknown jobs, and projects only one complete,
unique-class **constructed isolated serial job** to native Parquet. Random/RNFail
run through the existing runner. Independent exact references check its native
metrics, and reopening the learning checkpoint preserves one result row. This
example uses no cross-job learning and claims no observed CI timeline or savings.

Converted JSON contains source rows: keep recipe-only data local, outside public
commits and mirrors. The publisher validates exact cached source correspondence,
cache/output separation and output containment before immutable publication.
Identical concurrent retries converge; interrupted writes produce no completed
JSON. Process-kill temporary-file and filesystem durability limits are inherited
from the existing artifact writer. No separate experiment framework, learning
checkpoint, CLI dependency, MCP dependency or automatic download is introduced.



### FILE: docs/scenario-payoffs.md

# Signed scenario allocation for CI resources

Finite scenario allocation chooses among explicitly declared CI resource plans.
It is separate from finite coverage selection and from `PortfolioUCB`, which
selects learning policies. Signed modeled returns remain signed; neither a ranking,
a bounded reward nor a scenario weight is interpreted as calibrated evidence.

The API evaluates complete alternatives over shared joint scenarios, checks
resources/risk separately, and returns exact conditional forecasts and an auditable
choice. It executes no allocation and mutates no holdings. Native CI scheduling,
NAPFD/APFDc and RNFail remain unchanged.

## Complete synthetic CI fixture

```python
from decimal import Decimal

from coleman.allocation import (
    AllocationLimits, AllocationProblem, CurrentAllocation, DiscreteAllocation,
    JointScenario, NamedAmount, ProbabilityEvidence, ResourceCapacity,
    RiskConstraints, ScenarioPayoff, SignedPayoff, select_allocation,
)
from coleman.results.domain import fingerprint
from coleman.selection import Quantity, UnitSemantics

credit = UnitSemantics(unit="credit", meaning="synthetic-ci-credit-accounting-v1")
seconds = UnitSemantics(unit="s", meaning="modeled-serial-ci-resource-time-v1")

def amount(value, semantics=credit):
    return Quantity(value=Decimal(value), semantics=semantics)

def signed(value):
    return SignedPayoff(value=Decimal(value), semantics=credit)

states = ("idle", "busy")
gross = {"no_action": ("0", "0"), "stable": ("2", "2"), "variable": ("10", "-8")}
durations = {"no_action": "0", "stable": "3", "variable": "4"}

def action(name):
    return DiscreteAllocation(
        action_id=name, holdings=(),
        resource_use=(NamedAmount(name="runner_time", amount=amount(durations[name], seconds)),),
        capital_required=amount("0"), transaction_cost=amount("0"),
        gross_payoffs=tuple(
            ScenarioPayoff(scenario_id=state, gross=signed(value))
            for state, value in zip(states, gross[name], strict=True)
        ),
    )

problem = AllocationProblem(
    schema_version=1,
    data_fingerprint=fingerprint({
        "gross": {name: list(values) for name, values in gross.items()},
        "durations": durations, "probabilities": ["0.5", "0.5"],
    }),
    value_semantics=credit, initial_balance=amount("10"),
    current=CurrentAllocation(
        holdings=(), reserved_balance=amount("0"),
        resource_use=(NamedAmount(name="runner_time", amount=amount("0", seconds)),),
    ),
    holding_definitions=(),
    resources=(ResourceCapacity(name="runner_time", capacity=amount("5", seconds)),),
    scenarios=tuple(JointScenario(scenario_id=state, probability=Decimal("0.5")) for state in states),
    probability_evidence=ProbabilityEvidence(kind="assumed"),
    actions=tuple(action(name) for name in gross), no_action_id="no_action",
    risk=RiskConstraints(downside_target=signed("0")),
)
result = select_allocation(problem, limits=AllocationLimits(deadline_seconds=None))
assert result.choice.selected_action_id == "stable"
assert result.choice.status == "optimal"
forecasts = {row.forecast.action_id: row.forecast for row in result.completed}
assert forecasts["variable"].expected_net.value == Decimal("1")
assert forecasts["variable"].variance.value == Decimal("81")
```

Credits are synthetic modeled units, not currency or measured CI savings. All fees
are zero in this fixture, so its gross increments equal the issue's net payoffs:

| Plan | Joint net increments | Expected net | Variance | Expected shortfall below 0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no_action | 0, 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| stable | 2, 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| variable | 10, -8 | 1 | 81 | 4 |

The negative scenario remains in the result. If all changed plans have negative
expected net and the unchanged plan returns zero, `no_action` is optimal. If every
feasible plan loses, the least-bad modeled optimum can still be negative.

## Accounting roles and complete input

Each modeled accounting amount carries explicit units and versioned meaning;
the example uses a generic CI credit accounting context. The roles are distinct:

- `initial_balance`: initial modeled stock, not an expected payoff;
- `current`: current complete holdings/resource vectors and reserved liquidity;
- `capital_required`: liquidity reserved for an alternative, including fee funding;
- `transaction_cost`: one deterministic expense per action, charged once;
- `gross_payoffs`: the entire target allocation's joint-state increment before that fee;
- `net = gross - transaction_cost` and `terminal_balance = initial_balance + net`.

Reserved capital is **not another expense** and is not subtracted from terminal
balance. Holdings are explicit target quantities, not an automatic valuation or
additional return transformation. A producer must define whole-plan gross
increments consistently with its accounting context. Scenario-varying fees,
automatic holding valuation and implicit financing are outside this v1 contract.

Every action must include every declared resource/holding component, even if its
amount is zero. Omitted/extra components and unit/meaning mismatches fail rather
than becoming free or unavailable quantities. Resources are total chosen-plan use,
including current commitments; their ceilings are inclusive. The fee must be funded
by reserved liquidity, and a plan's reservation must fit initial balance to be
feasible. A structurally valid plan exceeding a resource/capital ceiling is a
rejected alternative, not a malformed forecast.

`no_action_id` identifies a required explicit action preserving current holdings,
resource use and reservation with zero new transaction cost. Its gross increments
are declared; existing commitments can have nonzero/negative outcomes. The unchanged
choice is not assumed feasible if its actual modeled constraints fail.

## Joint weights, units and exact definitions

Each action declares exactly one gross payoff for every joint scenario ID. Joining
is by ID, so changing row order cannot scramble correlated outcomes. A bundled
plan's joint gross increment already represents the complete plan; the API does
not add independent marginal variances or manufacture scenarios from seeds.

Scenario probabilities carry dimensionless unit `1` and explicit joint-probability
meaning. They are finite nonnegative decimals with at most twelve fractional
places and must sum **exactly to one (tolerance zero)**. Zero-probability states
retain their raw outcomes. Malformed weights are rejected and never silently
renormalized; producers own any explicitly versioned estimation/rounding procedure.

For net payoff `X`, target `T`, and weights `p`, the exact summaries are:

- expected net: `sum(p * X)`;
- population scenario variance: `sum(p * X^2) - sum(p * X)^2`, in squared payoff units;
- expected target shortfall: `sum(p * max(T - X, 0))`, in payoff units.

Target shortfall is an unconditional positive-part expectation, **not CVaR** or a
tail-conditioned confidence measure. Risk ceilings optionally constrain variance,
expected target shortfall and minimum terminal balance in every positive-point-weight
scenario. A null ceiling means that constraint was not requested. Raw negative
outcomes remain visible when the alternative is infeasible.

`UtilitySpec(kind="expected_net")` maximizes expected signed net. For nonlinear
utility use `quadratic_target` and a nonnegative coefficient `c` with the inverse
payoff semantics returned by `penalty_semantics(value_semantics)`:

```python
from coleman.allocation import UtilitySpec, penalty_semantics

utility = UtilitySpec(
    kind="quadratic_target",
    coefficient=amount("0.1", penalty_semantics(credit)),
)
```

This evaluates `sum(p * (X - c * max(T-X,0)^2))`, in payoff units. It is not utility
of the mean. For `[12,-6]`, equal weights and `T=0,c=0.1`, expected net is 3 but
expected utility is 1.2; a stable return 2 is preferred. Missing/unused coefficients
and incompatible inverse/squared units fail validation, including for zero values.

Input amounts/holdings/resources and signed gross increments are bounded by
`10^12` units with twelve decimal places. Integer arithmetic retains products at
24/48 fractional places; exact outputs allow 48 fractional and 110 total digits,
bounded by `10^48`. Decisions have **zero arithmetic rounding tolerance** and do
not depend on process Decimal precision. Equivalent decimal spellings/signed zero
serialize canonically. Continuous optimization, log utility, CVaR and unspecified
nonconvex objectives are explicitly unsupported; unknown objective kinds fail.

## Assumptions, estimated weights and conservative choices

`ProbabilityEvidence(kind="assumed")` declares a conditional model assumption,
not verified real-world calibration. `optimal` means the exact best feasible
alternative in this complete supplied finite model. It does not certify external
universe completeness, forecast accuracy, independent observations or production CI
value. Exact ties favor `no_action`, then ascending action ID.

Estimated weights require evidence fingerprint/method ID and lower/upper bounds
for every joint scenario. Bounds must contain the point weights; no statistical
confidence/coverage is assigned automatically. Independent-unit/count metadata may
be explicitly unknown; a supplied count requires a named observation unit. Zero
is not used for an unknown count, and repeated seeds
never become independent observations.

The selector retains estimated weights, bounds and conditional forecasts but
returns `insufficient_evidence`. It can select only the unchanged action when its
capital/resources and risk can be conservatively certified over declared support.
For this fallback, variance is bounded by squared payoff range, target shortfall
by the largest supported shortfall, and terminal floors are checked in every
state with positive probability upper bound. These loose support bounds apply to
every normalized distribution there; failure to certify is not proof of
infeasibility. If no fallback is certified, selection is null. Nothing activates a
new plan merely because its point estimate is favorable.

External evidence or undisclosed scenarios cannot be authenticated by a hash.
Use [protected evaluation](protected-evaluation.md) to justify empirical assumptions;
declaring a weight source never substitutes for a scientific evaluation protocol.

## Execution limits, checkpoints and result evidence

`AllocationLimits` bounds new action examinations, overall cooperative seconds and
estimated additional working bytes. Input caps are 64 discrete actions, 256 joint
scenarios and 64 resource/holding components. No-action is evaluated first; remaining
IDs are canonical. One work unit is one attempted whole-action evaluation. Deadline
polling also occurs between scenario operations. An interrupted action contributes
no partial forecast, while completed evaluations and the best incumbent survive.
Zero work can produce no incumbent; this is `limited`, not fabricated infeasibility.

The timer starts at API entry and never resets per phase. Validation/checkpoint
replay/output/serialization have bounded overhead. The deadline is cooperative,
not a hard process kill; the memory preflight is an estimate, not measured RSS,
and excludes already supplied input, interpreter and artifact payload. Malformed
inputs and unexpected callback errors propagate. Keyboard interruption during
search returns complete progress with explicit termination status.

`AllocationResult` embeds the complete source, limits/preflight, checkpoint input,
completed evaluations, exact forecasts/risk rejections and a separate `choice`.
Reading/serialization recomputes every reported forecast/check from joint evidence
and verifies choice, scope completion and work accounting. A forged utility,
feasibility, selected ID or falsely complete enumeration is rejected.

| Choice status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `optimal` | Every finite action checked, best feasible under assumed point weights |
| `feasible` | Best complete incumbent during interrupted/limited enumeration |
| `infeasible` | Full declared model checked; no feasible alternative |
| `limited` | Preflight or execution left no complete feasible incumbent |
| `insufficient_evidence` | Estimated weights; only a certified no-action fallback is allowed |

`termination_reason` separately records `enumeration_complete`, work/deadline,
cancellation/interruption or memory preflight. Null selection is not zero payoff.
Negative/inconclusive results are valid artifacts. No bounded-reward normalization
or learning reward is produced.

`result.checkpoint()` exports versioned complete evaluations, including rejected
alternatives. Store the JSON with existing `CheckpointPayload.extra` and
`LocalCheckpointStore` (trusted local pickle state). Resume with
`select_allocation(problem, checkpoint=...)`; source and each cached row are checked
before early preflight returns. Verified rows do not consume new search units;
verification overhead can repeat computation and is not a performance claim.
Cached rows still poll deadline/cancellation, including fully completed checkpoints.
Stopping that invocation preserves its explicit termination reason and verified
cached evidence: a previously complete optimum remains mathematically optimal,
without falsely reporting that this invocation completed enumeration.
Changed/future/corrupt checkpoints fail rather than inventing progress.

`publish_allocation_result(result, ArtifactWriter(root))` immutably publishes exact
JSON under `allocation-results/<content-digest>.json`; existing manifests inventory
it. Identical concurrent publication is idempotent. Existing local hard-link/fsync
and power-loss limits apply; incomplete writes expose no completed JSON. The core
does not write files unless this adapter is explicitly called.

`allocation_record(result, run_id=..., available_at=...)` projects selected modeled
summaries to existing #251 sinks. Exact JSON is authoritative; each projected
meaning ends in `binary64-projection-v1` and identifies a modeled quantity. Signed
losses remain negative, variance has squared units, and no selection yields
unavailable measurements. Supply actual zoned availability after calculation and
retain it on retries. Native `cost`/APFDc and rewards are not reinterpreted.

## Installed native CI examples

```bash
pip install path/to/coleman.whl
python ci.py ./ci-output
python resources.py ./resource-output
```

Copy [ci.py](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/examples/scenario-payoffs/ci.py)
or [resources.py](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/examples/scenario-payoffs/resources.py)
outside the repository before running; outputs remain within the invocation
directory. The CI example freezes the synthetic model, selects `stable`, maps its
declared three-second resource plan into the actual native fixed-time runner, and
verifies native scheduling before publishing the separate plan record. Native
Greedy/RNFail/NAPFD/Parquet components are real and unchanged. The resolved RunSpec
retains source, limits, result identity and adapter version. Repeated publication
uses a committed domain record's availability timestamp and checks identical content.
Legacy native-row retry semantics remain unchanged. The resource example evaluates
synthetic runner-slot alternatives; neither example claims measured savings or
policy superiority.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    State[Explicit current holdings, resources and initial balance] --> Problem[Versioned finite joint-scenario problem]
    Payoffs[Signed whole-plan gross increments and one fee] --> Problem
    Weights[Assumed weights or estimated weights with bounds] --> Problem
    Problem --> Guard[Shared work timer and memory preflight]
    Guard --> Forecast[Exact scenario moments and pointwise utility]
    Forecast --> Check[Separate capital, resource and risk checks]
    Check --> Choice[Conditional best complete action]
    Weights --> Evidence[Insufficient evidence for estimated weights]
    Evidence --> Fallback[Certified unchanged fallback or null]
    Choice --> Result[Self-contained exact result and completed evidence]
    Fallback --> Result
    Result --> Artifacts[Existing ArtifactWriter, manifests and local sinks]
    Result --> Checkpoint[Verified progress in existing checkpoint store]
    Checkpoint --> Guard
    Choice --> Native[Existing native CI runner example]
```

## Compatibility and limits

Problem/result/checkpoint artifacts require integer `schema_version=1` and supported
`allocation-v1` semantics. Missing/old/future versions, duplicate JSON keys, unknown
fields, mismatched units and forged evidence fail closed. No migration invents
weights, fees, holdings, uncertainty or execution history. Existing native,
coverage and protected-evaluation artifact bytes retain their contracts; shared
decimal conversion keeps its twelve-place default and adds exact product scales.

This finite offline model provides mathematical decisions, not a market connector,
live execution, learned probability calibration or continuous allocation engine.
Independent mathematical/performance benchmarking remains #255; broader CI
generalization needs protected evaluation and diversified-corpus evidence.

::: coleman.allocation



### FILE: docs/setup.md

# Setup & Architecture

## Default run (no Docker required)

Coleman is framework-first: the default installation works without any
external services. Use Python 3.14 or later in an activated virtual environment.
Install this repository's GitHub release wheel, pinned to its published SHA-256.
Pip verifies the complete wheel against this digest before installation:

```bash
python -m pip install "https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.10.0/coleman-4.10.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=b85b6d94fdb48d7f31d580583dfe1be96de2c63f07341b7159d2fbf777639d29"
```

Use the library API or the `coleman` CLI to run experiments:

```python
from coleman.api import run, load_spec

spec = load_spec("my-experiment.yaml")
result = run(spec)
print(result.run_id, result.artifacts_dir)
```

```bash
coleman run --config my-experiment.yaml
```

Results are written as **partitioned Parquet files** (zstd compressed) under
`./runs/` by default.  You can query them directly with DuckDB or Polars
without loading everything into RAM.

Repeated runs append new result files by default. They do not replace previous
results unless you explicitly remove `./runs/` or choose another `out_dir`.

## Architecture overview

Coleman separates three concerns:

| Layer | Purpose | Default | Optional |
|-------|---------|---------|----------|
| **Results** | Persist experiment facts (NAPFD, APFDc, …) | Partitioned Parquet | DuckDB sink, ClickHouse sink |
| **Checkpoints** | Crash-safe resume | Local filesystem (pickle + progress.json) | — |
| **Telemetry** | Observability (latency, throughput) | Disabled (NoOp) | OpenTelemetry + Collector |

### Null adapters

When a layer is disabled its module resolves to a **Null implementation**
with near-zero overhead:

* `NullSink` — discards result rows
* `NullCheckpointStore` — never saves/loads checkpoints
* `NoOpTelemetry` — all instrument calls are instant no-ops

## Configuration system

For registered, bounded CI workflows, the [application API and optional local MCP
tools](application-api.md) share native services across library, CLI and tool
clients. This capability is available in COLEMAN 4.x and adds no dependency to the
base installation. Its bounded session lifecycle is separate from direct native
runner checkpoint continuation.

Coleman uses **YAML configuration files** validated against typed
Pydantic v2 models.  See the [Configuration guide](configuration.md) for
the full schema reference, config packs, sweep engine, and determinism
contract.

### Quick example

```yaml
# experiment.yaml
packs:
  - policy/linucb
  - reward/rnfail
  - results/parquet

experiment:
  datasets: ["alibaba@druid"]

execution:
  independent_executions: 30
```

```bash
coleman run --config experiment.yaml
```

### Key concepts

| Concept | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **RunSpec** | Typed Pydantic v2 model describing one complete experiment run |
| **Config packs** | Composable YAML fragments (`packs/<category>/<name>.yaml`) merged left-to-right |
| **Sweep engine** | Grid (Cartesian) or zip (paired) expansion of parameter ranges into multiple specs |
| **Deterministic run_id** | `sha256(canonical_json(spec))[:12]` — same config always produces the same ID |
| **Provenance** | `spec.resolved.json` + `provenance.json` (git, Python version, `uv.lock` hash) per run |

## Optional extras

```bash
# Telemetry (OpenTelemetry SDK)
python -m pip install "coleman[telemetry] @ https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.10.0/coleman-4.10.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=b85b6d94fdb48d7f31d580583dfe1be96de2c63f07341b7159d2fbf777639d29"

# ClickHouse sink
python -m pip install "coleman[clickhouse] @ https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.10.0/coleman-4.10.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=b85b6d94fdb48d7f31d580583dfe1be96de2c63f07341b7159d2fbf777639d29"
```

## Optional observability stack

See the [Observability guide](observability.md) for a Docker Compose stack
with OTel Collector + Grafana (ClickHouse under a profile).

## How to query results

Results are written as Hive-partitioned Parquet files under `./runs/`.  You
can query them directly with DuckDB (already a project dependency):

```sql
-- Average NAPFD per policy
SELECT policy, AVG(fitness) AS avg_napfd
FROM read_parquet('./runs/**/*.parquet', hive_partitioning=1)
GROUP BY policy
ORDER BY avg_napfd DESC;

-- Cost distribution per reward function
SELECT reward_function,
       PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cost) AS median_cost
FROM read_parquet('./runs/**/*.parquet', hive_partitioning=1)
GROUP BY reward_function;
```

For a guided end-to-end walkthrough, see the official [workflow notebook](workflow.py).

## Additive measurement artifacts

The native result schemas remain unchanged. See [versioned domain results](domain-results.md)
for the typed observation contract, Mermaid commit/recovery diagram and local-sink
sidecars that join to CI decisions without replacing the runner or checkpoint store.



### FILE: docs/workflow.md

# Coleman Workflow

This page covers the full operational loop for running and analyzing
experiments.  Each section maps to a cell in the interactive
[marimo notebook](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/blob/main/docs/workflow.py)
([docs/workflow.py](workflow.py)) — open it locally with `marimo edit docs/workflow.py`
for a live, executable version.

Download options for the notebook source:

- Browser raw view: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/main/docs/workflow.py
- Direct download with curl:

```bash
curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/main/docs/workflow.py -o workflow.py
```

- Direct download with wget:

```bash
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/main/docs/workflow.py -O workflow.py
```

---

## 1 — Active Configuration

Read the runtime configuration from `run.yaml`:

```python
import yaml
from pathlib import Path

config_path = Path("run.yaml")
with open(config_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
    config = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}

results_cfg = config.get("results", {})
checkpoint_cfg = config.get("checkpoint", {})
telemetry_cfg = config.get("telemetry", {})
experiment_cfg = config.get("experiment", {})
```

Key settings you should inspect:

| Setting                  | Where it comes from                  |
|--------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| `datasets`               | `experiment.datasets`                |
| `budget.mode`            | `experiment.budget.mode`             |
| `budget.values`          | `experiment.budget.values`           |
| `results.enabled`        | `results.enabled`                    |
| `results.sink`           | `results.sink` (parquet / clickhouse)|
| `results.out_dir`        | `results.out_dir`                    |
| `checkpoint.enabled`     | `checkpoint.enabled`                 |
| `checkpoint.base_dir`    | `checkpoint.base_dir`               |
| `telemetry.enabled`      | `telemetry.enabled`                  |
| `telemetry.otlp_endpoint`| `telemetry.otlp_endpoint`            |

---

## 2 — Code Cost Evaluation

Coleman measures code cost as a **multi-dimensional scorecard**
with four dimensions:

| Dimension        | What it measures                      | Tools                  |
|------------------|---------------------------------------|------------------------|
| **Structural**   | Maintainability, complexity, change risk | Radon, Xenon, Wily  |
| **Runtime**      | CPU time, hotspots, memory pressure   | Scalene, py-spy        |
| **Energy**       | Estimated energy / carbon impact      | CodeCarbon, pyRAPL     |
| **Operational**  | Infrastructure effort proxy           | All of the above       |

### Structural cost — CI gates

Two gates run in CI on every pull request:

```bash
# Xenon complexity gate
python -m xenon --max-absolute C --max-modules B --max-average A coleman/

# Radon maintainability index (MI) — lists modules below the threshold;
# CI fails if this command reports such modules or exits with an error
python -m radon mi -s -n B coleman/
```

### Running code cost checks locally

```bash
# All structural checks (complexity + maintainability + xenon gate)
make cost-structural

# Runtime profiling with Scalene
make cost-profile-scalene

# Energy estimation with CodeCarbon
make cost-energy

# Complexity trend analysis with Wily
make cost-wily
```

See [Code Cost Evaluation](code-cost.md) for full documentation.

---

## 3 — Live Observability

Grafana is where you inspect live execution behavior:

- **Grafana:** [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000)
- **OTel collector endpoint:** configured via `telemetry.otlp_endpoint`

Use it for throughput, latency, CPU, memory, worker isolation,
dataset slicing, and execution separation while the run is active.

---

## 4 — Resume / Recovery State

Inspect checkpoint progress files used for resume and recovery:

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path

checkpoint_root = Path(checkpoint_cfg.get("base_dir", "checkpoints"))
checkpoint_files = sorted(checkpoint_root.glob("**/progress_*.json"))

for f in checkpoint_files:
    payload = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    print(f"  {f.parent.name}: step={payload.get('step_committed')}")
```

---

## 5 — Final Results Storage

Final experiment facts are stored in the results sink, not in Grafana.

- **Parquet root:** configured via `results.out_dir` (default `./runs`)
- **ClickHouse sink:** enabled only when `results.sink = "clickhouse"`
- Re-running experiments in the same `runs` directory appends new Parquet
  files by default. Existing result files are preserved.

### Loading results with DuckDB

```python
import duckdb

parquet_glob = "./runs/**/*.parquet"

summary_df = duckdb.sql(f"""
    SELECT scenario,
           execution_id,
           experiment,
           policy,
           reward_function,
           AVG(fitness) AS avg_napfd,
           AVG(cost) AS avg_apfdc,
           AVG(prioritization_time) AS avg_prioritization_time,
           AVG(process_memory_rss_mib) AS avg_rss_mib,
           AVG(process_cpu_utilization_percent) AS avg_cpu_pct,
           MAX(wall_time_seconds) AS wall_time_seconds
    FROM read_parquet('{parquet_glob}', hive_partitioning=1)
    GROUP BY scenario, execution_id, experiment, policy, reward_function
    ORDER BY avg_napfd DESC, avg_apfdc DESC
""").df()
```

---

## 6 — Export

Export the current summary as a CSV artifact for reports:

```python
export_dir = runs_root / "analysis"
export_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
summary_df.to_csv(export_dir / "summary.csv", index=False)
```

---

## 7 — Analysis Plot

Plot average NAPFD per policy from the persisted final results:

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

top_policies = (
    summary_df
    .groupby("policy", as_index=False)["avg_napfd"]
    .mean()
    .sort_values("avg_napfd", ascending=False)
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))
sns.barplot(data=top_policies, x="policy", y="avg_napfd", ax=ax)
ax.set_title("Average NAPFD by Policy")
ax.set_xlabel("Policy")
ax.set_ylabel("Average NAPFD")
ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
```

---

## 8 — Runner Extensions (hooks + extensions)

When you need custom domain workflows without replacing Coleman orchestration,
add `hooks` and `extensions` in YAML:

```yaml
hooks:
  fail_fast: false
  plugins:
     - my_project.hooks.ForecastHook

extensions:
  my_domain:
     forecast_selection:
        policy: ThompsonSampling
        reward: Binary
```

Recommended lifecycle contract:

- Run and dataset hooks in coordinator process
- Execution hooks in worker process
- Keep hook code idempotent and free of global mutable state
- Emit custom artifacts under each run directory when possible

`on_error` is emitted for execution-start failures and environment
construction failures, not only for failures inside the main run body.

---

## 9 — Advanced Analyses You Can Run

Coleman now ships built-in analysis reports aligned with the analysis playbook.

```bash
# Quality ranking (NAPFD)
coleman analyze quality --input ./runs --format markdown --out reports/quality.md

# Stability (coefficient of variation)
coleman analyze stability --input ./runs --format csv --out reports/stability.csv

# Pareto frontier (quality vs cost)
coleman analyze pareto --input ./runs --format table
```

Supported report modules:

1. `quality`
2. `cost`
3. `stability`
4. `pareto`
5. `sensitivity`
6. `resources`

Use this checklist after generating enough runs:

1. **Policy stability**
    - Compare mean, std, and coefficient of variation of NAPFD per policy.
2. **Quality vs cost frontier**
    - Build a Pareto frontier using high NAPFD + low APFDc.
3. **Budget sensitivity**
    - Compare policies per `scenario` / time-ratio group.
4. **Execution variance**
    - Track variance between independent executions for the same policy/reward.
5. **Operational footprint**
    - Compare memory and CPU metrics versus quality gains.
6. **Custom extension impact**
    - Group by extension-related dimensions (from custom artifacts) and compare uplift.

See the complete guide in [analysis-playbook.md](analysis-playbook.md).

---

## 10 — Full Extensibility in Practice

Coleman supports full orchestration customization patterns. Use this quick map:

1. `hooks` + `extensions`
    - Best option for domain logic without rewriting runner flow.
2. New `Policy` and `Reward`
    - Native extension model through module exports + YAML selection.
3. Custom `EvaluationMetric` and `Environment`
    - Source-level extension path for deeper runtime behavior changes.

Parallel-safe implementation guidance:

1. Keep execution hooks worker-local and idempotent.
2. Keep run/dataset hooks coordinator-local for aggregation and reporting.
3. Persist custom artifacts with `run_id` + `execution_id` so analyses can join safely across parallel runs.

Complete implementation details and end-to-end examples:

- [extensibility.md](extensibility.md)

## Query Snippets

### DuckDB

```sql
SELECT scenario, execution_id, policy, AVG(fitness) AS avg_napfd
FROM read_parquet('./runs/**/*.parquet', hive_partitioning=1)
GROUP BY scenario, execution_id, policy
ORDER BY avg_napfd DESC;
```

### ClickHouse

```sql
SELECT scenario, execution_id, policy, AVG(fitness) AS avg_napfd
FROM coleman_results
GROUP BY scenario, execution_id, policy
ORDER BY avg_napfd DESC;
```

---

## Result Persistence Semantics

- Parquet appends new files under `./runs/`
- ClickHouse appends new rows to `coleman_results`
- `execution_id` is the safest way to isolate one run analytically
- Checkpoints update the latest durable state for the same run and experiment
- If you want a fresh analytical space, clean `./runs/` and optionally `./checkpoints/`

---

## Suggested Next Steps

- Run `coleman run --config run.yaml` to generate fresh experiment data
- Run `make cost-structural` to evaluate structural cost before and after changes
- Run `make cost-energy` to compare energy impact of different implementations
- Open Grafana to inspect live execution behavior while the run is active
- Use the Parquet summary above for final comparisons and report export
- Inspect `./checkpoints/` to verify resume and recovery progress
- Switch to ClickHouse when you want a persistent analytical store instead of Parquet files

### FILE: docs/zip64-source-selection.md

# Bounded ZIP64 selected-file integrity

**COLEMAN 4.8** adds an explicit ZIP64 recipe to the existing verified source
cache through [#314](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/pull/314) for
[#301](https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/issues/301).
The feature verifies selected-file membership and supports the
[real RTPTorrent Parquet/replay workflow](rtptorrent-parquet-etl.md).
Legacy package-v1 ZIP behavior remains unchanged.

## Run the owned CI example outside the checkout

Install the verified published wheel in Python 3.14+, then download the exact
release-tagged example and verify its SHA-256. Its two executions are offline
and need no foreign dataset, Docker or MCP SDK:

```bash
uv venv /tmp/coleman-zip64-env --python 3.14
uv pip install --python /tmp/coleman-zip64-env/bin/python "https://github.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/releases/download/v4.10.0/coleman-4.10.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=b85b6d94fdb48d7f31d580583dfe1be96de2c63f07341b7159d2fbf777639d29"
mkdir -p /tmp/coleman-zip64-workspace
cd /tmp/coleman-zip64-workspace
curl --fail --location --output ci.py \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jacksonpradolima/coleman/v4.10.0/examples/zip64-selection/ci.py
/tmp/coleman-zip64-env/bin/python -c 'import hashlib, sys; from pathlib import Path; sys.exit(0 if hashlib.sha256(Path("ci.py").read_bytes()).hexdigest() == "cf0a610bfa4a620f7620c5b02c5c36c667adaa801839d48a5a6dbd044814cf05" else "Example SHA-256 mismatch")'
/tmp/coleman-zip64-env/bin/python ci.py selected /tmp/coleman-zip64-cache
/tmp/coleman-zip64-env/bin/python ci.py selected /tmp/coleman-zip64-cache
```

The example creates actual ZIP64 local-size and end records around a tiny owned
CI correctness fixture, including an `owned@ci/serial.json` logical member name.
It verifies the enclosing SHA-256, all archive header identities, selected decoded
SHA-256/size and actual deflate EOF/CRC. It persists the canonical recipe and raw
child receipt only after the selection succeeds. Both invocations converge on the
same bytes and identities. This fixture establishes functional correctness, not
independent observations or evidence of production savings.

Reopen the same verified selection from that workspace without a reader or network:

```python
from pathlib import Path

from coleman.corpus import SourceCache
from coleman.corpus.zip64_contracts import Zip64SelectionSpec
from coleman.corpus.zip64_selection import materialize_zip64_files, validate_zip64_files

spec = Zip64SelectionSpec.from_json(Path("selected/selection.json").read_bytes())
cache = SourceCache("/tmp/coleman-zip64-cache")
validate_zip64_files(spec, cache)
receipts = materialize_zip64_files(spec, cache)
assert cache.member_path(receipts[0], "serial.json").is_file()
```

The installed-package regression test also consumes the actual selected fixture
with the native TCPCI runner, compares NAPFD/APFDc with the existing independent
tiny oracle, and reopens committed checkpoints. No ZIP64 parser, materializer or
native runner is mocked in that workflow.

## Contract and bounds

`Zip64SelectionSpec` requires integer `schema_version=1` and recipe
`bounded-zip64-file-selection-v1`. Missing, future and unknown versions reject.
Canonical JSON and fingerprints include the complete source, member pins, reviewed
data terms and explicit limits. Selections sort by logical member name; changing
archive bytes changes enclosing identity even when selected child bytes agree.

| Quantity | Meaning and hard limit |
| --- | --- |
| Enclosing source | Complete raw archive bytes; at most 8 GiB, with explicit source/member/total limits above the existing smaller defaults |
| Directory | At most 4,096 entries and 2 MiB metadata, checked before allocating standard-library ZIP objects |
| Selection | 1–128 distinct regular files; at most 64 MiB decoded bytes per file and in total |
| Paths | Portable ASCII logical names, up to 1,024 characters, with safe `@` labels; never filesystem extraction paths |
| Framing | Single disk, fixed ZIP64 end payload, stored or deflated members, reviewed local/central sizes and offsets, signed or unsigned data descriptors |

All byte counts are strict nonnegative integers. Zero is a valid empty selected
file when its SHA-256 and actual bytes agree; null, negative and non-integer byte
counts reject. An unavailable source is an acquisition failure, not a zero-byte
source. Versions, offsets, flags, CRC and exact sentinel-dependent ZIP64 extras
must agree. Duplicate/aliased names, links, special entries, traversal, prefixes,
encryption, unsupported compression and malformed metadata reject.

ZIP structures follow the [PKWARE ZIP specification](https://pkware.cachefly.net/webdocs/casestudies/APPNOTE.TXT),
with the deliberately narrower profile above and two explicitly reviewed producer
forms observed in RTPTorrent: stored entries may retain bit 1 as an inert
compression preference, and offset-only ZIP64 central metadata may retain legacy
extraction version 1.0/2.0. Bits 1/2 have no defined compression meaning for stored
payloads in the specification; only the observed bit 1 is accepted here. Local and
central flags still must agree exactly; size sentinels still require version 4.5
and both local size fields. A lower local version is accepted against central
version 4.5 only when the actual central offset was sentinel-backed and neither
central size used a sentinel. Resolving that wide offset to a small value does
not erase its origin. Offset-only metadata still requires the exact wide offset
and ZIP64 end records. Legacy profiles keep rejecting these forms.
This is not a general ZIP extractor.
Unselected payloads are not decoded or CRC-certified. Their local/central header
identities and physical bounds are checked; the entire enclosing byte stream is
still covered by its frozen source SHA-256.

## Provenance, failures and compatibility

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Explicit reader + frozen opaque source recipe] --> B[Existing raw materializer and external SourceCache]
    B --> C[Verify complete enclosing SHA-256 and size]
    C --> D[Bound ZIP64 footer and central metadata]
    D --> E[Check every central and local header identity]
    E --> F[Decode only selected files; verify EOF, CRC, SHA-256 and byte count]
    F --> G[Existing immutable raw child cache and receipts]
    G --> H[Retain full ZIP64 recipe with all child receipts]
    H --> I[Separate parser, ETL and scientific admission]
```

The enclosing raw source and every child use the existing `MaterializationSpec`.
Selected archive names bind to explicit portable raw-file aliases. Child bytes,
data terms and version must match their enclosing selection. Data redistribution
terms do not assert rights to execute or redistribute enclosed subject code.
Source URIs are descriptive; the core opens no URL and imports no CLI/MCP or HTTP
transport. Readers are explicit, synchronous and caller-owned.

An interrupted acquisition never publishes a partial blob. A later child failure
may leave individually verified earlier blobs, but the operation returns no
completed selection. Retrying revalidates actual membership even for cached
children and converges through existing immutable writes. There is no new group
completion marker or learning checkpoint: callers retain the full recipe with all
returned receipts. A raw child receipt alone does not prove enclosing membership.
`validate_zip64_files` verifies source, membership and cached children without
repair or network; missing/corrupt bytes reject. Complete validation scans the
large source again, so account for that I/O cost.

Metadata/format/hash/CRC failures raise `ValueError`; filesystem/reader failures
propagate. Cache parents must be trusted and immutable during verification.
Existing ArtifactWriter local-filesystem durability limits apply; this is neither
a hostile-filesystem sandbox nor a global cache/disk quota.

Existing package-v1 and selected-member-v1 recipes retain their ZIP64 and `@`
rejections. No old recipe or receipt is silently migrated or reinterpreted.
Construct and review a separate ZIP64 recipe with full source/member pins; old
native Parquet, result records and checkpoints remain readable as before.

## External source evidence

The [RTPTorrent assessment](rtptorrent.md) records the provider metadata and
separately verified HikariCP member bytes. Complete acquisition on 2026-10-16
verified all **5,016,963,482 source bytes**, provider MD5
`1f7fa822b0cf155bd007a94d1a24a336`, and complete source SHA-256:

```text
bff52563d75aee2f4bab9693188cdefbfd887dc4bcf63395d49eaff1ecf7b6c1
```

The actual materializer then checked all 2,883 central/local records, decoded the
pinned HikariCP member, reverified offline and repeated idempotently. The existing
raw-class reader converted **46,995 observations across 1,662 source jobs**,
retaining 23,302 repeated class executions and 1,530 jobs without reported class
failures/errors. These are descriptive source counts, not independent projects,
verified full-job passes or temporal admission. No third-party rows/code are
bundled in the wheel or repository.

The wheel includes only the reviewed metadata recipe
`rtptorrent-hikaricp-zip64-selection-v1.json`. It pins the complete archive,
2,825,388 decoded member bytes and the data-record CC BY 4.0 terms. The conservative
`recipe_only` redistribution declaration does not relicense enclosed subject code.
The data record and [specific license text](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode.txt)
remain the terms evidence; selected data conversion is separate from permission
to execute a subject repository.

For an actual source acquisition, work outside checkout with the installed wheel:

```bash
cd /tmp/coleman-zip64-workspace
curl --fail --retry 3 --continue-at - --max-time 21600 \
  --output rtp-torrent-v11.zip \
  https://zenodo.org/records/4046180/files/rtp-torrent-v11.zip
```

This explicit operator download can resume on retry; it is not a cache completion
receipt. The following core operation verifies the full frozen source SHA-256
before accepting any member. Existing small-source HTTP adapter budgets remain
unchanged. Keep the approximately 5 GB archive and cache outside Git and separate
from published outputs.

```python
from importlib.resources import files
from pathlib import Path

from coleman.corpus import SourceCache
from coleman.corpus.zip64_contracts import Zip64SelectionSpec
from coleman.corpus.zip64_selection import materialize_zip64_files, validate_zip64_files

resource = files("coleman.corpus.resources").joinpath("rtptorrent-hikaricp-zip64-selection-v1.json")
spec = Zip64SelectionSpec.from_json(resource.read_bytes())
cache = SourceCache("/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-source-cache")
receipts = materialize_zip64_files(spec, cache, lambda: Path("rtp-torrent-v11.zip").open("rb"))
validate_zip64_files(spec, cache)
assert materialize_zip64_files(spec, cache) == receipts
csv_path = cache.member_path(receipts[0], "hikaricp-class-results.csv")
assert csv_path.stat().st_size == 2825388
```

This is real source acquisition and selected-member validation. The
[Parquet workflow](rtptorrent-parquet-etl.md) adds complete analytical history,
a bounded native projection and a declared replay bridge in #302.
Protected temporal evaluation remains blocked by missing source clocks and
logical build/job mapping. A fresh installed-wheel regression can additionally
reverify the real source cache without network:

```bash
COLEMAN_RTPTORRENT_ZIP64_REAL_CACHE=/tmp/coleman-rtptorrent-source-cache \
  uv run pytest tests/corpus/test_installed_zip64.py --no-cov -q
```
